documentVariables.summary: Keeps named values that any number box can use, written in curly braces such as {width} / 2, so one change updates every field that uses them.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: Name of the new variable: letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.

fields.name: Value
fields.text: A number, or a formula using other variables such as {width} / 2 + 1.

fields.name: Add
fields.text: Adds the new variable to the list.

fields.name: Variables
fields.text: The list of variables; edit a name or value in place, it saves when you leave the box.

fields.name: Delete
fields.text: Removes that variable.

fields.name: Export...
fields.text: Saves the variables to a text file.

fields.name: Import...
fields.text: Loads variables from a text file; ones with the same name are replaced.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Type a name and a value, then press Add.
In any number box, type the variable in curly braces, such as {depth} + 1.
Or right click a number box to insert a variable.

jobSetup.summary: Changes the kind of job, the material size and thickness, units, where zero is, and the 3D modeling resolution.

fields.name: Job Type
fields.text: Single Sided, Double Sided (cut from both faces) or Rotary (cut on a turning blank).

fields.name: Width (X)
fields.text: Width of the material.

fields.name: Height (Y)
fields.text: Height (length) of the material.

fields.name: Material Thickness (Z)
fields.text: Thickness of the material.

fields.name: Units
fields.text: Work in millimeters or inches.

fields.name: Blank Shape
fields.text: Rotary only: a round Cylinder or a Square blank.

fields.name: Blank Length
fields.text: Rotary only: length of the blank along its axis.

fields.name: Blank Diameter
fields.text: Rotary only: diameter of a round blank; reads Blank Side for a square one.

fields.name: Blank Along
fields.text: Rotary only: whether the blank lies along the X axis or the Y axis.

fields.name: Flip design with the material when the axis changes
fields.text: Rotary only: turns the design with the blank when you change its axis.

fields.name: Flip Direction
fields.text: Double sided only: how the material is turned over, left-right or top-bottom.

fields.name: Bottom Side Z Zero
fields.text: Double sided only: where Z zero is when cutting the bottom face.

fields.name: Z Zero Position
fields.text: Where Z zero is: Material Surface or Machine Bed; for rotary, Center of Rotation or Blank Surface.

fields.name: XY Datum Position
fields.text: Which point of the material is X0, Y0: a corner or the center.

fields.name: Use Offset
fields.text: Moves the datum away from that point by the offsets below.

fields.name: Datum Offset X
fields.text: How far the datum is moved in X.

fields.name: Datum Offset Y
fields.text: How far the datum is moved in Y.

fields.name: Scale design with job size
fields.text: Shown when the job has a design: stretches vectors and components to the new size.

fields.name: Modeling Resolution
fields.text: Finer keeps small detail on big jobs but makes 3D work slower; Standard suits most jobs.

fields.name: Material Settings
fields.text: Picks the color or texture the material shows in the 3D view.

fields.name: OK
fields.text: Applies the job setup.

fields.name: Cancel
fields.text: Closes without changes.

steps: Pick the job type.
Enter the material size and thickness and pick the units.
Set where Z zero and the XY datum are, to match how you zero the machine.
Press OK.

drawRectangle.summary: Draws a rectangle or square, with square, rounded or inward-curved corners. Drag it out in the 2D view or type its size and position.

fields.name: Anchor Point
fields.text: Picks which point of the rectangle (a corner, an edge middle or the center) X and Y place.

fields.name: X
fields.text: Horizontal position of the anchor point.

fields.name: Y
fields.text: Vertical position of the anchor point.

fields.name: Corner Type
fields.text: Square corners, corners rounded outward (Radiused External) or curved inward (Radiused Internal).

fields.name: Radius
fields.text: Size of the rounded corners; only used when the corner type is not Square.

fields.name: Width (X)
fields.text: Width of the rectangle across the job.

fields.name: Height (Y)
fields.text: Height of the rectangle up the job.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Shown when shapes are selected for editing: changes them to the values above.

fields.name: Create
fields.text: Draws a new rectangle with the values above.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form; rectangles already drawn stay.

steps: Pick the corner type and, for rounded corners, a radius.
Click and drag in the 2D view to draw the rectangle, or type the anchor, width and height.
Press Create (or Enter) to make a rectangle from the typed values.
Drag the green corner handles to change the radius before creating.

drawCircle.summary: Draws a circle from its center and its radius or diameter. Drag it out in the 2D view or type the values.

fields.name: Center X
fields.text: Horizontal position of the circle's center.

fields.name: Center Y
fields.text: Vertical position of the circle's center.

fields.name: Size
fields.text: Choose whether the size box below is the Radius or the Diameter.

fields.name: Radius
fields.text: Distance from the center to the edge; reads Diameter when Diameter is picked.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Shown when circles are selected for editing: changes them to the values above.

fields.name: Create
fields.text: Draws a new circle with the values above.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form; circles already drawn stay.

steps: Click the center in the 2D view and drag out the radius, or type the center and size.
Press Create (or Enter) to draw from the typed values.
To change an existing circle, click it, edit the values and press Apply.

drawEllipse.summary: Draws an ellipse from its width and height. Drag it out in the 2D view or type its size and position.

fields.name: Anchor Point
fields.text: Picks which point of the ellipse's box (a corner, an edge middle or the center) X and Y place.

fields.name: X
fields.text: Horizontal position of the anchor point.

fields.name: Y
fields.text: Vertical position of the anchor point.

fields.name: Width (X)
fields.text: Overall width of the ellipse.

fields.name: Height (Y)
fields.text: Overall height of the ellipse.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Shown when ellipses are selected for editing: changes them to the values above.

fields.name: Create
fields.text: Draws a new ellipse with the values above.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form; ellipses already drawn stay.

steps: Click and drag in the 2D view to draw the ellipse, or type the anchor, width and height.
Press Create (or Enter) to draw from the typed values.
To change an existing ellipse, click it, edit the values and press Apply.

drawPolygon.summary: Draws a regular polygon with any number of equal sides, such as a hexagon or octagon.

fields.name: Center X
fields.text: Horizontal position of the polygon's center.

fields.name: Center Y
fields.text: Vertical position of the polygon's center.

fields.name: Number of Sides
fields.text: How many sides the polygon has, for example 6 for a hexagon.

fields.name: Size
fields.text: Choose whether the size box below is the Radius or the Diameter.

fields.name: Radius
fields.text: Distance from the center to a corner; reads Diameter when Diameter is picked.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Shown when polygons are selected for editing: changes them to the values above.

fields.name: Create
fields.text: Draws a new polygon with the values above.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form; polygons already drawn stay.

steps: Set the number of sides.
Click the center in the 2D view and drag out the size, or type the center and size.
Press Create (or Enter) to draw from the typed values.

drawStar.summary: Draws a star from its number of points, its outer radius and how deep its inner corners go.

fields.name: Number of Points
fields.text: How many points the star has, for example 5.

fields.name: Center X
fields.text: Horizontal position of the star's center.

fields.name: Center Y
fields.text: Vertical position of the star's center.

fields.name: Outer Radius
fields.text: Distance from the center to the tip of each point.

fields.name: Inner Radius (% of outer)
fields.text: Depth of the inner corners as a percentage of the outer radius; lower makes thinner points.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Shown when stars are selected for editing: changes them to the values above.

fields.name: Create
fields.text: Draws a new star with the values above.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form; stars already drawn stay.

steps: Set the number of points and the inner radius percentage.
Click the center in the 2D view and drag out the outer radius, or type the values.
Press Create (or Enter) to draw from the typed values.

drawPolyline.summary: Draws a line point by point, with straight spans or smooth curves. Click points in the 2D view or type each next point.

fields.name: Enter the next point as
fields.text: Type the next point as X, Y, as an angle and length, or as dX, dY from the last point.

fields.name: Next Point X
fields.text: X of the next point; reads X Offset when entering dX, dY.

fields.name: Next Point Y
fields.text: Y of the next point; reads Y Offset when entering dX, dY.

fields.name: Angle
fields.text: With Angle and Length: direction of the next span from the last point, in degrees.

fields.name: Length
fields.text: With Angle and Length: how long the next span is.

fields.name: Add
fields.text: Adds the typed point to the line; Enter in a box does the same.

fields.name: Undo
fields.text: Removes the last point added.

fields.name: Finish
fields.text: Ends the line; it needs at least two points.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Click in the 2D view to place points; click and drag to make a smooth curve.
Or type the next point and press Add.
Click the start point (or press Tab) to close the shape.
Press Finish or Space to end an open line.

drawArc.summary: Draws an arc through points you click, or from typed start and end points and a radius or height.

fields.name: Arc Type
fields.text: Click the arc as start, end and a point on it, or as center, start and end.

fields.name: Start Point
fields.text: X and Y where the arc begins.

fields.name: End Point
fields.text: X and Y where the arc ends.

fields.name: Size By
fields.text: Set the typed arc by its Radius or by its Height above the line from start to end.

fields.name: Radius
fields.text: Radius or height of the typed arc; a negative value puts it on the other side.

fields.name: Create
fields.text: Draws the arc from the typed values.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form; arcs already drawn stay.

steps: Pick the arc type.
Click the points in the 2D view in the order the hint shows.
Or type the start and end points, pick Radius or Height, enter the size and press Create.

dimensions.summary: Adds dimension lines to the drawing: lengths, horizontal or vertical distances, angles and arc radii.

fields.name: Dimension Type
fields.text: Pick Length, Vertical, Horizontal, Angle or Arc; the clicks and fields change to suit.

fields.name: First Point
fields.text: X and Y of the points the dimension measures; the boxes shown depend on the type.

fields.name: Radius
fields.text: Arc type only: the radius of the arc or circle being dimensioned.

fields.name: Show Diameter
fields.text: Arc type only: shows the diameter instead of the radius.

fields.name: Use Custom Text
fields.text: Shows your own text instead of the measured value.

fields.name: Custom Text
fields.text: The text to show when Use Custom Text is ticked.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Shown while editing a dimension picked with Shift click: saves its new points and text.

fields.name: Font
fields.text: Font used for the text of new dimensions.

fields.name: Text Height
fields.text: Height of the dimension text.

fields.name: Decimal Places
fields.text: How many decimal places the value shows (angles have their own setting).

fields.name: Offset
fields.text: Gap between the measured point and the start of each extension line.

fields.name: Place Dimensions on Layer
fields.text: Puts new dimensions on their own layer instead of the active one.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: Name of the layer dimensions go on.

fields.name: Create
fields.text: Makes a dimension from the typed values.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Pick the dimension type.
Click the points in the 2D view in the order the hint lists; the last click places the line or text.
Or type the points and press Create.
Shift click an existing dimension to edit it, or drag its text to move the line.

drawFreehand.summary: Sketches a vector by dragging the mouse; when you let go the stroke is smoothed into curves.

fields.name: Smoothness
fields.text: Low follows the stroke closely; high rounds corners into curves with fewer nodes.

fields.name: Stabilize
fields.text: Higher values damp out hand jitter: the line trails behind the pointer inside a circle.

fields.name: End vector at cursor
fields.text: Carries the line on to where the pointer is when you let go, not where the brush lagged.

fields.name: Fade Selected Bitmap
fields.text: Shown with a picture selected: fades it in the 2D view so your strokes stand out.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form; strokes already drawn stay.

steps: Set the smoothness and stabilizing sliders.
Hold the mouse button down in the 2D view and drag to sketch.
Finish near the start, or press Tab while drawing, to close the shape.
Hold Ctrl when starting on the end of an open vector to carry it on.

traceBitmap.summary: Traces the dark areas, or chosen colors, of a picture into closed vectors laid exactly over it.

fields.name: Colors
fields.text: Color pictures only: sets how many colors the picture is split into.

fields.name: Trace
fields.text: Picks the color whose areas are traced; you can also click the color on the picture.

fields.name: Link
fields.text: Traces this color together with the picked one as a single area.

fields.name: Reset
fields.text: Clears all Link ticks.

fields.name: Trace Area
fields.text: Drag over the picture to trace only part of it; click it to trace all of it.

fields.name: Threshold
fields.text: Black and white pictures: pixels darker than this (0 to 255) are traced; 128 is middle gray.

fields.name: Noise Filter
fields.text: Drops specks smaller than this many pixels in area; raise it for grainy pictures.

fields.name: Corner Fit
fields.text: Fit outlines with straight Lines or smooth Curves.

fields.name: Corner Fit slider
fields.text: Loose smooths the outline more; Tight follows the pixels more closely.

fields.name: Bitmap Fading
fields.text: Fades the picture in the 2D view so the traced vectors are easier to see.

fields.name: Preview
fields.text: Shows the traced outlines without making them.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Makes the traced vectors.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Import a picture and select it in the 2D view.
Set the threshold, or pick the color to trace for a color picture.
Adjust Noise Filter and Corner Fit, then press Preview to check.
Press Apply to make the vectors.

move.summary: Moves the selection to an exact position, or by a set distance from where it is.

fields.name: Anchor Point
fields.text: Absolute moves only: which point of the selection box goes to X and Y.

fields.name: Type of Move
fields.text: Absolute places the anchor at X, Y; Relative shifts the selection by X, Y.

fields.name: X Position
fields.text: The X position (Absolute) or the distance to move across (Relative).

fields.name: Y Position
fields.text: The Y position (Absolute) or the distance to move up or down (Relative).

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Moves the selection.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the objects to move.
Pick Absolute or Relative.
For Absolute, pick the anchor point; then type X and Y.
Press Apply.

setSize.summary: Sets an exact width and height for the selection, as a whole or for each item on its own.

fields.name: Mode
fields.text: Scale the selection as one block, or scale each selected item individually.

fields.name: Anchor Point
fields.text: The point of the selection box that stays put while it changes size.

fields.name: Width
fields.text: New width of the selection.

fields.name: Height
fields.text: New height of the selection.

fields.name: Link XY
fields.text: Keeps the proportions: changing one size changes the other to match.

fields.name: Auto Scale Z
fields.text: With components selected: changes their height in proportion with their new size.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Resizes the selection.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the objects to resize.
Pick the mode and the anchor point that should stay put.
Type the new width or height; leave Link XY ticked to keep proportions.
Press Apply.

rotate.summary: Turns the selection by an angle, or to an exact angle, about a pivot point.

fields.name: Pivot Point
fields.text: Turn about a corner or the center of the selection, or about typed coordinates.

fields.name: Pivot X
fields.text: With Use Coordinates: X of the point to turn about.

fields.name: Pivot Y
fields.text: With Use Coordinates: Y of the point to turn about.

fields.name: Type of Rotation and Angle
fields.text: Relative turns by the angle; Absolute sets the selection to that angle.

fields.name: Angle
fields.text: Angle in degrees; positive turns counterclockwise.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Rotates the selection.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the objects to rotate.
Pick the pivot point, or click in the 2D view to place it.
Pick Relative or Absolute and type the angle.
Press Apply.

mirror.summary: Flips the selection across its own center or edges, the material center, or a straight line you pick.

fields.name: Horizontal
fields.text: Flips the selection left to right about its own center.

fields.name: Vertical
fields.text: Flips the selection top to bottom about its own center.

fields.name: Left Edge
fields.text: Flips across the left edge of the selection box.

fields.name: Right Edge
fields.text: Flips across the right edge of the selection box.

fields.name: Top Edge
fields.text: Flips across the top edge of the selection box.

fields.name: Bottom Edge
fields.text: Flips across the bottom edge of the selection box.

fields.name: Left to Right
fields.text: Flips left to right about the center of the material.

fields.name: Top to Bottom
fields.text: Flips top to bottom about the center of the material.

fields.name: Flip About Line
fields.text: Flips across a straight line picked last with Shift click.

fields.name: Create a mirrored copy
fields.text: Leaves the original in place and flips a copy instead.

fields.name: Use Rotated Bounds
fields.text: For a single rotated object: flips about its own turned box, not the upright one.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the objects to flip.
Tick Create a mirrored copy to keep the original.
Click the button for the flip you want; it happens at once.

distort.summary: Bends the selected vectors, text or a component, by dragging an envelope around them or by fitting them to curves.

fields.name: Mode
fields.text: Bounding Box drags an envelope; Along a Single Curve or Between Two Curves fits to open vectors.

fields.name: Bake Components
fields.text: Shown when several components are selected: combines them into one so they can be distorted.

fields.name: Use Rotated Bounds
fields.text: Starts the envelope from the turned box of a rotated selection.

fields.name: Bake Distortion
fields.text: Makes the distortion permanent so the vectors can be node edited.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Curve modes: bends the objects along the curve or curves selected last.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the objects; for the curve modes select the open vector or vectors last.
Pick the mode.
Bounding Box: drag the envelope nodes in the 2D view; I adds a node, D deletes one.
Curve modes: press Apply.
Press Bake Distortion when you are happy with the shape.

vectorUnwrapper.summary: For rotary jobs: unrolls a closed cross-section into a flat profile once round the blank, for use in a two rail sweep.

fields.name: Center of Rotation
fields.text: Unroll about the center of the contour, the center of the job or a custom point.

fields.name: X
fields.text: Custom point only: X of the center of rotation.

fields.name: Y
fields.text: Custom point only: Y of the center of rotation.

fields.name: Refine unwrapped vectors
fields.text: Simplifies the result into far fewer nodes.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Makes the unrolled profile as a new vector.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Set the job type to Rotary in Job Setup.
Select one closed cross-section contour.
Pick the center of rotation; for a custom point drag the round handle or type it.
Press Apply.

align.summary: Lines up the selection on the material or on the last selected object, and spaces objects evenly.

fields.name: Align to Material
fields.text: Centers the selection on the material, both ways or in X or Y only.

fields.name: Align to Selection
fields.text: Lines the objects up with the last one selected: centers, edges, or just outside top or bottom.

fields.name: Space Selection
fields.text: Spaces the objects evenly across or up; Ctrl click keeps the order they were selected.

fields.name: Inside last vector
fields.text: Spaces the objects inside the last selected vector instead of across their own span.

fields.name: Show common tools on drawing tab
fields.text: Also shows the main align buttons on the Design tab.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the objects; select the one to align to last.
Click an align or space button; it acts at once.
Ctrl click a space button to keep the order you selected them in.

snapSettings.summary: Chooses what the pointer snaps to in the 2D view, and sets the grid, snap reach and nudge distance.

fields.name: Snap to nodes
fields.text: Snaps to the points of vectors.

fields.name: Snap to midpoints
fields.text: Snaps to the middle of spans.

fields.name: Snap to centers
fields.text: Snaps to the centers of arcs and circles.

fields.name: Snap to intersections
fields.text: Snaps to where vectors cross.

fields.name: Snap to job corners and center
fields.text: Snaps to the corners and center of the material.

fields.name: Snap to guides
fields.text: Snaps to guide lines.

fields.name: Snap to grid
fields.text: Snaps to the grid points.

fields.name: Smart snapping
fields.text: Snaps the pointer into line with points of nearby objects as you draw.

fields.name: Grid spacing
fields.text: Distance between grid points.

fields.name: Snap radius (px)
fields.text: How close, in screen pixels, the pointer must be to snap; about 10 works well.

fields.name: Snap distances (drags move in round steps for the zoom)
fields.text: Makes drags move in round steps that suit the zoom level.

fields.name: Fixed nudge distance
fields.text: How far Ctrl+Shift with an arrow key moves the selection.

fields.name: OK
fields.text: Saves the settings and closes the form.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes without saving.

sculpt.summary: Shapes the selected component by hand in the 3D view: smooth, smudge, add or take away material with a brush.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: The brush: Smooth, Smudge, Deposit (adds), Remove (takes away) or Undo Brush (puts back the start).

fields.name: Use a custom brush
fields.text: Deposit and Remove only: stamps the shape of another component or a brush file instead of a round brush.

fields.name: Brush
fields.text: The component or loaded brush file used as the custom brush.

fields.name: Load Brush...
fields.text: Loads a brush from a file or picture.

fields.name: Angle
fields.text: Turns the custom brush by this many degrees.

fields.name: Dynamic Rotation
fields.text: Turns the custom brush to follow the direction of the stroke.

fields.name: Merge
fields.text: Merges each stroke with earlier ones instead of piling them on top.

fields.name: Diameter
fields.text: Size of the brush; the mouse wheel changes it too.

fields.name: Strength
fields.text: How much each stroke changes the surface; around 50% is a gentle start.

fields.name: Smoothness
fields.text: Softness of the brush edge: 0 is a hard edge, higher fades out toward the rim.

fields.name: Preserve Transparency (0)
fields.text: Keeps the brush inside the component's outline; off lets it build on empty areas.

fields.name: Show Visible Model (F)
fields.text: Shows the whole model while sculpting, not just the selected component.

fields.name: Mode
fields.text: Normal lets heights rise or fall; Raise only lets them go up; Lower only lets them go down.

fields.name: Overlay image opacity
fields.text: Shown with an overlay picture: how strongly it shows over the model.

fields.name: Show overlay image (O)
fields.text: Shows or hides the overlay picture.

fields.name: Preset
fields.text: Picks saved brush settings for this tool.

fields.name: Add
fields.text: Saves the current brush settings as a named preset.

fields.name: Remove
fields.text: Deletes the chosen preset.

fields.name: Keep
fields.text: Marks the sculpting so far as a point Discard goes back to.

fields.name: Discard
fields.text: Throws away the sculpting since the last Keep.

fields.name: OK
fields.text: Finishes sculpting and keeps the changes.

fields.name: Cancel
fields.text: Throws away all sculpting done since the form opened.

steps: Select one component in the Components list.
Pick a tool and set the diameter and strength.
Drag over the model in the 3D view to sculpt.
Press Keep at good points; press OK when done.

guidePosition.summary: Sets the exact position of a guide line, locks it, or deletes it.

fields.name: Position
fields.text: Where the guide sits: X for a vertical guide, Y for a horizontal one.

fields.name: Lock this guide
fields.text: Stops the guide being dragged by accident.

fields.name: Delete Guide
fields.text: Removes the guide.

fields.name: OK
fields.text: Moves the guide to the typed position.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes without changes.

join.summary: Joins selected open vectors whose ends are close enough into single vectors.

fields.name: Join Tolerance
fields.text: Ends closer than this are joined; keep it small, such as 0.1 mm.

fields.name: Join
fields.text: Joins the selected open vectors.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the open vectors to join.
Set the join tolerance.
Press Join.

offset.summary: Draws a new outline a set distance outside or inside the selected vectors.

fields.name: Direction
fields.text: Outwards (right of an open vector) or Inwards (left of an open vector).

fields.name: Distance
fields.text: How far the new outline sits from the original.

fields.name: Create sharp offset corners
fields.text: Keeps outside corners sharp instead of rounding them.

fields.name: Offset
fields.text: Makes the offset outline.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the vectors.
Pick the direction and type the distance.
Press Offset.

fillet.summary: Rounds corners, or adds dog-bone and T-bone reliefs so a round cutter can reach inside corners.

fields.name: Tool Radius
fields.text: Radius of the fillet; for reliefs, use the radius of the cutter.

fields.name: Fillet Type
fields.text: Normal rounds the corner; Dog-Bone, T-Bone and Plasma / Drag Knife cut reliefs or loops.

fields.name: OK
fields.text: Closes the form; fillets already made stay.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Set the tool radius and fillet type.
Click a corner in the 2D view to fillet it.
Click an existing fillet to take it out again.

trim.summary: Removes spans of vectors back to the nearest crossings by clicking on them.

fields.name: Rejoin Trimmed Sections
fields.text: When the form closes, joins the trimmed pieces whose ends meet.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Click a span in the 2D view; it is cut back to the nearest crossings.
Hold the button down and drag over spans to trim several.
Ungroup grouped vectors first; groups cannot be trimmed.

trimObjects.summary: Cuts the selected objects at a closed boundary vector, clearing what lies inside or outside it.

fields.name: Trim Options
fields.text: Clear the parts inside the boundary, or the parts outside it.

fields.name: Refit Curves After Clipping
fields.text: Smooths the cut vectors back into curves after trimming.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Trims the objects.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the objects to trim.
Shift select the closed boundary vector last.
Pick inside or outside and press Apply.

measure.summary: Measures the distance and angle between two points, or reads the details of a span or a whole vector.

fields.name: Measure
fields.text: Between 2 Points gives distance and angle; Span and Contour Properties give length, area and more.

fields.name: Clear
fields.text: Clears the current measurement.

fields.name: OK
fields.text: Closes the form.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Pick what to measure.
For two points, click both points, or press and drag; snapping applies.
For a span or contour, click the vector.

editPicture.summary: Adjusts the brightness, contrast and look of the selected picture, and can add a faded border.

fields.name: Contrast
fields.text: Makes darks darker and lights lighter; negative flattens the picture.

fields.name: Brightness
fields.text: Lightens or darkens the whole picture.

fields.name: Gamma
fields.text: Brightens or darkens the middle tones; 1 leaves them as they are.

fields.name: Invert
fields.text: Swaps light and dark.

fields.name: Grayscale
fields.text: Removes the color.

fields.name: Border type
fields.text: No border, a rectangular border or an oval border.

fields.name: Fade width
fields.text: How wide the border fades out, as a percentage of the picture.

fields.name: Reset
fields.text: Puts the sliders back to their starting values.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Applies the changes to the picture as one undo step.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select one picture in the 2D view.
Move the sliders and tick the options you want.
Press Apply.

vectorTexture.summary: Fills the selected closed vectors, or the whole job, with rows of straight or wavy lines to machine as a texture.

fields.name: Angle
fields.text: Direction of the rows, from -90 to 90 degrees.

fields.name: Max. Spacing
fields.text: Largest distance between two rows.

fields.name: Spacing variation
fields.text: 0% keeps rows evenly spaced; higher makes the gaps random.

fields.name: Wavelength
fields.text: Length of one wave along a row.

fields.name: Amplitude
fields.text: Height of the waves either side of the row; 0 keeps rows straight.

fields.name: Noise
fields.text: Adds a random wobble to the rows; 0% is smooth.

fields.name: Place Vectors on Layer
fields.text: Puts the texture lines on their own layer.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: Name of the layer for the texture lines.

fields.name: Preview
fields.text: Shows the lines dashed without making them.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Makes the texture lines.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select closed vectors to fill, or none for the whole job.
Set the angle, spacing and wave settings.
Press Preview to check, then Apply.

extend.summary: Stretches the end of an open vector in a straight line until it meets another vector, or meets another end's extension.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Click the end of an open vector; a dashed extension line appears.
Click where the extension meets a span, or click the end of another open vector to meet its extension.
Right click to start again with a different end.

fitCurves.summary: Replaces vectors made of many short spans with fewer smooth arcs, curves or straight lines.

fields.name: Fitting Type
fields.text: Fit with Circular Arcs, Bezier Curves or Straight Lines.

fields.name: Tolerance
fields.text: How far the new vector may stray from the old one; smaller is closer but uses more spans.

fields.name: Keep Sharp Corners
fields.text: Keeps corners sharp instead of rounding them into the fit.

fields.name: Max Angle
fields.text: Corners that turn by more than this many degrees stay sharp.

fields.name: Replace selected vectors
fields.text: Replaces the originals; off keeps them and puts the fitted copies on the current layer.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Fits the selected vectors.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the vectors to fit.
Pick the fitting type and set the tolerance.
Press Apply.

validator.summary: Checks vectors for open ends, crossings, duplicates and zero length spans that stop them cutting cleanly, and marks each problem.

fields.name: V-Groove Mode
fields.text: Ignores crossings inside text, which fonts often have and V-groove copes with.

fields.name: Search Selected Vectors
fields.text: Searches the selection, or all visible vectors when nothing is selected; press again to Stop.

fields.name: Marks
fields.text: Key to the marks drawn in the 2D view for each kind of problem.

fields.name: Fix zero length Spans
fields.text: Removes the zero length spans that were found, then searches again.

fields.name: Show
fields.text: Selects the vector with that problem and zooms to it.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the vectors to check, or none to check them all.
Press the search button.
Press Show next to a problem to zoom to it, then fix it.
Press Fix zero length Spans if any were found.

boundary.summary: Draws one closed outline around the selected objects, optionally grown outward or stretched round them like a rubber band.

fields.name: Offset Boundary
fields.text: Grows the outline outward by the distance below.

fields.name: Distance
fields.text: How far outside the objects the outline sits.

fields.name: Rubber Band Boundary
fields.text: Stretches the outline round the objects, bridging gaps and hollows.

fields.name: Create
fields.text: Makes the boundary vector.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the objects.
Tick the options you want and set the distance.
Press Create.

arrayCopy.summary: Copies the selection into a grid of rows and columns, with optional mirroring and staggered rows or columns.

fields.name: Selected Objects Size
fields.text: Shows the width and height of the selection, to help set the spacing.

fields.name: Columns (X)
fields.text: How many copies across, including the original.

fields.name: Rows (Y)
fields.text: How many copies up, including the original.

fields.name: Spacing By
fields.text: Gap is the space between copies; Offset is the distance from one copy's start to the next.

fields.name: X
fields.text: Gap or offset between columns.

fields.name: Y
fields.text: Gap or offset between rows.

fields.name: Block Symmetry
fields.text: Click each copy in the two by two block to mirror or turn it; the pattern repeats.

fields.name: Row X
fields.text: Every other row shifts this far across, for a staggered or brick pattern.

fields.name: Row Y
fields.text: Every other row shifts this far up or down.

fields.name: Column X
fields.text: Every other column shifts this far across.

fields.name: Column Y
fields.text: Every other column shifts this far up or down.

fields.name: Group Copies
fields.text: Groups the copies together.

fields.name: Copy
fields.text: Makes the copies.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the vectors or components to copy.
Set the columns and rows.
Pick Gap or Offset and set the X and Y spacing.
Press Copy.

nest.summary: Packs the selected parts onto one or more sheets with little waste, leaving room for the cutter between them.

fields.name: Tool Dia. (D)
fields.text: Diameter of the cutter that will cut the parts out.

fields.name: Clearance (C)
fields.text: Extra gap kept between parts on top of the tool diameter.

fields.name: Border Gap
fields.text: Space kept clear around the edge of each sheet.

fields.name: Rotate Parts to find best fit
fields.text: Lets parts turn to fit better.

fields.name: Rotation Step
fields.text: Angle steps the parts may turn by, such as 90 degrees.

fields.name: Mirror parts to find best fit
fields.text: Lets parts be flipped to fit better.

fields.name: Allow parts inside other parts
fields.text: Lets small parts go in the holes of bigger ones.

fields.name: Remove original parts
fields.text: Deletes the originals once they are nested.

fields.name: Nest two-sided parts
fields.text: Double-sided jobs: objects on the other side move with each part.

fields.name: Nest From
fields.text: The corner of the sheet nesting starts from.

fields.name: Nest Direction
fields.text: Fill the sheet along X or along Y first.

fields.name: Nest boundary layer
fields.text: Nests inside the vectors on this layer instead of on the whole material.

fields.name: Number of copies
fields.text: How many of the selected part to nest.

fields.name: Filler
fields.text: Makes the selected part fill the space left after the others are placed.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Saves the copies and filler setting on the selected parts.

fields.name: Active Sheet
fields.text: The sheet to nest onto.

fields.name: Customize...
fields.text: Picks several sheets, and how many of each, to nest across.

fields.name: Nest
fields.text: Packs the parts.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the parts to nest.
Set the tool diameter, clearance and border gap.
Optionally set copies or Filler for some parts and press Apply.
Choose the sheet options and press Nest.

plates.summary: Copies a selected template across the material to make many plates, filling !!name!! text variables from a data file or a counter.

fields.name: Sheet Margins
fields.text: Space left clear at the edges of the material.

fields.name: Equal margins
fields.text: Uses one margin for all four edges; untick to set each edge.

fields.name: Horizontal
fields.text: Gap between plates across.

fields.name: Vertical
fields.text: Gap between plates up.

fields.name: Create each plate on its own sheet
fields.text: Puts every plate on a separate sheet.

fields.name: Create toolpaths (for the toolpaths calculated on the template)
fields.text: Copies the template's toolpaths for each sheet of plates.

fields.name: Mode
fields.text: Plates that do not fit go on new Sheets, or on new Layers of this sheet.

fields.name: Plates to Make
fields.text: Without a data file: how many plates to make.

fields.name: Import from file...
fields.text: Loads a text data file; each row makes one plate.

fields.name: Clear
fields.text: Stops using the data file.

fields.name: Separator
fields.text: The character between columns in the data file.

fields.name: First row is column names
fields.text: Treats the first row of the file as headings, not as a plate.

fields.name: Variables
fields.text: For each !!name!! in the text, pick a data column or a Counter to fill it.

fields.name: Start
fields.text: Counter only: the first number.

fields.name: Increment
fields.text: Counter only: how much the number goes up each plate.

fields.name: Digits
fields.text: Counter only: pads the number with leading zeros to this many digits; 0 for none.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the plates.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Draw the template, with text such as !!name!! where values change, and select it.
Set the margins and spacing.
Import a data file, or set how many plates to make.
Pick a column or counter for each variable.
Press Calculate.

gadget.summary: Runs a gadget chosen from the Gadgets menu. Its settings depend on the gadget and are shown in groups.

fields.name: Settings
fields.text: The gadget's own options: numbers, check boxes, choices and text, as the gadget asks.

fields.name: Choose a tool
fields.text: Shown when the gadget cuts: picks a tool from the tool database.

fields.name: OK
fields.text: Runs the gadget, or updates the toolpath being edited.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Pick a gadget from the Gadgets menu.
Select anything the gadget asks for.
Fill in its settings and press OK.

circularArray.summary: Copies the selection around a center point, over a full circle or part of one.

fields.name: Selected Objects Size
fields.text: Shows the width and height of the selection.

fields.name: Center X
fields.text: X of the point the copies go around; you can also drag the center marker.

fields.name: Center Y
fields.text: Y of the point the copies go around.

fields.name: Rotate Copies
fields.text: Turns each copy to face around the center; off keeps them upright.

fields.name: Number of Items
fields.text: How many items in total, including the original.

fields.name: Angle
fields.text: Set the Total Angle the copies spread over, or the Step Angle between them.

fields.name: Total Angle
fields.text: Angle in degrees; reads Step Angle when that is picked. Use 360 for a full circle; copies run clockwise.

fields.name: Copy
fields.text: Makes the copies.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the objects to copy.
Place the center by typing it, dragging the marker or clicking in the 2D view.
Set the number of items and the angle.
Press Copy.

copyAlong.summary: Places copies of an object, or circles, at even spacing along one or more vectors.

fields.name: Copy
fields.text: Copy Object places the first selected object; Copy Circles places circles instead.

fields.name: Circle Diameter
fields.text: Copy Circles only: size of each circle.

fields.name: Spacing
fields.text: Space by a Number of copies, or by a Distance between copies.

fields.name: Copies
fields.text: How many copies go along each vector.

fields.name: Distance
fields.text: Distance along the vector from one copy to the next.

fields.name: Force even spacing
fields.text: Stretches the distance slightly so copies land on both ends.

fields.name: Align Objects to curve
fields.text: Turns each copy to follow the direction of the vector.

fields.name: Create Copies on new layer
fields.text: Puts the copies on a new layer.

fields.name: Reverse Direction
fields.text: Starts from the other end of the vector.

fields.name: Copy
fields.text: Makes the copies.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the object to copy first, then Shift select the vectors to copy along.
Pick copies or distance and set the value.
Press Copy.

createText.summary: Writes text as vectors in any installed font, placed at a point or fitted to fill a box.

fields.name: Mode
fields.text: Text places text at a point; Text in a Box stretches it to fill a box.

fields.name: Text
fields.text: The words to write; changes show at once.

fields.name: Fonts
fields.text: Show All fonts, or only Single Line fonts suited to engraving.

fields.name: Font
fields.text: The font to use; drag the corner of the list to make it bigger.

fields.name: Bold
fields.text: Uses the bold style of the font.

fields.name: Italic
fields.text: Uses the italic style of the font.

fields.name: Text Height
fields.text: Height of the letters; not shown in box mode, where the box sets the size.

fields.name: Alignment
fields.text: Lines up several lines of text to the left, center or right.

fields.name: X
fields.text: Text mode: X of the anchor point.

fields.name: Y
fields.text: Text mode: Y of the anchor point.

fields.name: Anchor
fields.text: Text mode: which point of the text sits at X, Y.

fields.name: Width
fields.text: Box mode: width of the box the text fills.

fields.name: Height
fields.text: Box mode: height of the box the text fills.

fields.name: Margin
fields.text: Box mode: space kept inside the box edges: None, Normal or Wide.

fields.name: Vertical Stretch
fields.text: Box mode: fill the height by spreading the lines or by making letters taller.

fields.name: Horizontal Stretch
fields.text: Box mode: fill the width with word gaps, letter spacing, letter width or letter size.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form; the text is already made.

steps: Click in the 2D view to place the text, or drag a box in box mode.
Type the text and pick a font and height.
Drag the square handle to move the text, or a round handle to arch it.
Click elsewhere to start new text, or press Close.

textSelection.summary: Fine-tunes a piece of text in the 2D view: letter spacing, line spacing and arching.

fields.name: OK
fields.text: Closes the form.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Click a piece of text.
Click between two letters to close them up; Shift click opens them out.
Click between two lines to change their spacing the same way.
Drag the top handle up or the bottom handle down to arch the text.

textOnCurve.summary: Lays a line of text along a selected vector, above, on or below it.

fields.name: Text Size
fields.text: Keep the text size, or scale the text to fill the whole curve.

fields.name: Text Spacing
fields.text: Spreads or tightens the letters along the curve, in percent.

fields.name: Text Position
fields.text: Puts the text above, on or below the curve.

fields.name: Text on other side
fields.text: Moves the text to the other side of the curve.

fields.name: Offset Distance
fields.text: Gap between the curve and the text.

fields.name: Text Alignment
fields.text: Starts the text at the left, center or right of the curve; not used when filling.

fields.name: Character Orientation
fields.text: Turn each letter to follow the curve, or keep letters upright.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Puts the text on the curve.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select one line of text and one vector.
Set the size, position and spacing.
Press Apply; drag in the 2D view to slide the text along the curve.

profileToolpath.summary: Cuts along the selected vectors, outside, inside or on the line, to cut parts out or cut grooves.

fields.name: Start Depth (D)
fields.text: Depth the cut starts at; 0 is the material surface.

fields.name: Cut Depth (C)
fields.text: How deep the cut goes; for a cut-out, the material thickness or a little more.

fields.name: Show advanced toolpath options
fields.text: Shows the last pass, tabs, ramps, leads, order, start and corner options.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: Select... picks a tool from the database; Edit... changes it for this toolpath only.

fields.name: Edit Passes...
fields.text: Shows how many passes reach the cut depth and lets you change their depths.

fields.name: Machine Vectors
fields.text: Cut Outside / Right, Inside / Left, or On the vector.

fields.name: Direction
fields.text: Climb or Conventional cutting; climb usually leaves a cleaner edge.

fields.name: Allowance Offset
fields.text: Leaves this much extra material on the part; negative cuts into it.

fields.name: Do Separate Last Pass
fields.text: Cuts a final light pass to clean up the edge.

fields.name: Allowance (A)
fields.text: Material the earlier passes leave for the last pass to remove.

fields.name: Reverse direction
fields.text: Runs the last pass the other way round.

fields.name: Add tabs to toolpath
fields.text: Leaves small bridges so parts stay held in the sheet.

fields.name: Length
fields.text: Length of each tab.

fields.name: Thickness
fields.text: Height of each tab above the bottom of the cut.

fields.name: Create 3D Tabs
fields.text: Makes sloped tabs the tool ramps over instead of flat steps.

fields.name: Edit Tabs...
fields.text: Places tabs automatically or by clicking on the vectors.

fields.name: Ramp
fields.text: Ramps the tool into the cut (Smooth, Zig Zag or Spiral) by a distance or angle, instead of plunging.

fields.name: Leads
fields.text: Adds a straight or curved lead in, and optionally out, on closed vectors.

fields.name: Order
fields.text: Orders to try for cutting the vectors; the fastest ticked one is used.

fields.name: Start At
fields.text: Where each cut starts: optimized, the vectors' own start points, or nearest a box point.

fields.name: Corners
fields.text: Sharpens external corners; with a V-bit, can also sharpen internal corners.

fields.name: Project toolpath onto 3D model
fields.text: Follows the model surface, measuring depths down from it.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Selector... picks vectors by filters so templates find them again.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: Name of the toolpath in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the toolpath.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the vectors to cut.
Set the start and cut depths.
Pick a tool and choose outside, inside or on.
Add tabs if the parts are cut free.
Press Calculate.

pocketToolpath.summary: Clears all the material inside closed vectors down to a depth, with one or more tools.

fields.name: Start Depth (D)
fields.text: Depth the pocket starts at; 0 is the material surface.

fields.name: Cut Depth (C)
fields.text: Depth of the pocket floor below the material surface.

fields.name: Tools
fields.text: Tools in cutting order; later tools clear only what earlier ones could not reach.

fields.name: Edit Passes...
fields.text: Shows how many passes reach the depth and lets you change them.

fields.name: Clear Pocket
fields.text: Offset follows the shape in rings; Raster cuts back and forth in lines.

fields.name: Cut Direction
fields.text: Climb or Conventional cutting.

fields.name: Raster Angle
fields.text: Raster only: angle of the lines, 0 is along X.

fields.name: Profile Pass
fields.text: Raster only: cut round the edge first, last or not at all.

fields.name: Ramp Plunge Moves
fields.text: Ramps the tool into each pass instead of plunging straight down.

fields.name: Distance
fields.text: Length of the ramp.

fields.name: Pocket Allowance
fields.text: Leaves this much material on the pocket walls; negative cuts wider.

fields.name: Use Vector Selection Order
fields.text: Cuts the pockets in the order the vectors were selected.

fields.name: Project toolpath onto 3D model
fields.text: Follows the model surface, measuring depths down from it.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Selector... picks vectors by filters so templates find them again.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: Name of the toolpath in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the toolpath.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the closed vectors to pocket.
Set the start and cut depths.
Add a tool, and smaller ones after it for tight corners if needed.
Pick Offset or Raster and press Calculate.

drillToolpath.summary: Drills a hole at the center of each selected closed vector, with optional pecking and dwell.

fields.name: Start Depth (D)
fields.text: Depth the drilling starts at; 0 is the material surface.

fields.name: Cut Depth (C)
fields.text: How deep each hole goes.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: Select... picks a drill; Edit... changes it for this toolpath only.

fields.name: Use Peck Drilling
fields.text: Drills in steps, lifting out between them to clear chips.

fields.name: Peck Depth (P)
fields.text: Depth of each peck; it is the tool's pass depth.

fields.name: Retract
fields.text: Lift right out above the start depth, or just above the previous peck.

fields.name: Retract Gap (R)
fields.text: How far above that height the drill lifts between pecks.

fields.name: Dwell at the bottom of each drill pass
fields.text: Pauses at the bottom of each pass.

fields.name: Dwell Time
fields.text: How long the pause lasts, in seconds.

fields.name: Use Vector Selection Order
fields.text: Drills the holes in the order the vectors were selected.

fields.name: Project toolpath onto 3D model
fields.text: Measures depths down from the model surface.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Selector... picks vectors by filters so templates find them again.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: Name of the toolpath in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the toolpath.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select circles or other closed vectors at the hole positions.
Set the depths and pick a drill.
Tick peck drilling for deep holes.
Press Calculate.

vgrooveToolpath.summary: Carves inside closed vectors with a V-bit, going deeper where the shape is wider, as for lettering and signs.

fields.name: Start Depth (D)
fields.text: Depth the carving starts at; 0 is the material surface.

fields.name: Flat Depth (F)
fields.text: Tick to limit the depth; wider areas are left flat at this depth.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: Select... picks a V-bit; Edit... changes it for this toolpath only.

fields.name: Use Clearance Tools
fields.text: Uses flat tools to clear the flat areas when Flat Depth is on.

fields.name: Clearance tools
fields.text: The clearance tools in cutting order; each clears what the one before could not reach.

fields.name: Tool-specific options
fields.text: For the picked clearance tool: strategy, raster angle, direction and ramping.

fields.name: Corner Sharpen
fields.text: For a V-bit after the first tool: follows into corners left uncut instead of pocketing.

fields.name: Use Vector Start Points
fields.text: Starts each cut at the vector's own start point.

fields.name: Use Vector Selection Order
fields.text: Carves the shapes in the order they were selected.

fields.name: Project toolpath onto 3D model
fields.text: Measures depths down from the model surface.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Selector... picks vectors by filters so templates find them again.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: Name of the toolpath in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the toolpath.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the closed vectors, such as text.
Pick a V-bit.
For wide shapes, tick Flat Depth and add a clearance tool.
Press Calculate.

inlayToolpath.summary: Cuts a V-bit pocket and a matching plug from the same closed vectors, so the plug can be glued in face down.

fields.name: Pocket Depth (D)
fields.text: How deep the pocket is carved.

fields.name: Glue Gap (G)
fields.text: Space left between the plug top and the pocket floor for glue.

fields.name: Surface Gap (S)
fields.text: Gap between the two boards once pressed; bigger leaves less plug board to cut away.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: Select... picks a V-bit or engraving tool for both parts.

fields.name: Use Clearance Tools
fields.text: Uses flat tools to clear the wider areas.

fields.name: Clearance tools
fields.text: The clearance tools in cutting order.

fields.name: Plug Destination Sheet
fields.text: The sheet the plug toolpath goes on.

fields.name: Plug Outer Boundary
fields.text: Clear the plug board to the Sheet Limits, or to a Vector Offset round the shapes.

fields.name: Boundary Offset
fields.text: Vector Offset only: how far outside the shapes the plug board is cleared.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: Base name; the two toolpaths get Pocket and Plug added.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the pocket and plug toolpaths.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the closed vectors of the inlay.
Set the pocket depth and the gaps.
Pick a V-bit and, if needed, clearance tools.
Choose the plug sheet and press Calculate.

mouldingToolpath.summary: Sweeps a cross-section profile along one or more drive rails to cut a molding.

fields.name: Drive Rail
fields.text: Select the rails first, then the profile last; the count of each shows here.

fields.name: Clear Rail
fields.text: Clears the selection so you can pick the rails again.

fields.name: Toolpath position in the material
fields.text: Slides the molding up or down within the material thickness.

fields.name: Gap Above Toolpath
fields.text: Material left above the top of the profile.

fields.name: Gap Below Toolpath
fields.text: Material left under the lowest point of the profile.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: Select... picks the finishing tool, usually a ball nose.

fields.name: Vary Stepover
fields.text: Spaces passes over the profile surface so steep parts get more passes.

fields.name: Skip Flat Regions
fields.text: Leaves out finishing passes over flats the clearance tool already cut.

fields.name: Use Larger Area Clearance Tool
fields.text: Roughs the molding out first with a bigger tool.

fields.name: Machine Flat Regions
fields.text: Lets the clearance tool cut wide flat parts of the profile to exact height.

fields.name: Ramp Plunge Moves
fields.text: Ramps the clearance tool into each level instead of plunging.

fields.name: Distance
fields.text: Length of the clearance tool's ramp.

fields.name: Machining Allowance
fields.text: Material the clearance tool leaves for the finishing tool.

fields.name: Create Sharp Corners
fields.text: Makes sharp mitered corners where the rail turns, instead of rounded ones.

fields.name: Boundary Offset
fields.text: How far the passes run past the sides of the profile.

fields.name: Use automatic boundary offset
fields.text: Sets the boundary offset from the tool size, to clean steep ends.

fields.name: Rail Selection
fields.text: Selector... picks the rails by filters.

fields.name: Profile Selection
fields.text: Selector... picks the profile by filters; needs automatic rail selection.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: Name of the toolpath in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the toolpath.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the drive rails, then Shift select the profile last.
Set the position in the material.
Pick the finishing tool and, if wanted, a clearance tool.
Press Calculate.

quickEngraveToolpath.summary: Engraves along the selected vectors at a fixed depth, and can fill closed shapes with lines.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: Select... picks an engraving tool, such as a diamond drag tool.

fields.name: Depth / Pressure
fields.text: How deep to engrave; for a drag tool, how far it is pressed in.

fields.name: Engrave
fields.text: Outline follows the vectors; Fill also fills closed shapes.

fields.name: Stepover
fields.text: Fill only: distance between fill lines.

fields.name: Fill pattern
fields.text: Fill only: straight Hatch lines or Offset rings.

fields.name: Hatch Angle
fields.text: Hatch only: angle of the fill lines.

fields.name: Cross Hatch
fields.text: Hatch only: adds a second set of lines across the first.

fields.name: Use Nose Cone
fields.text: For a tool with a sprung nose cone: every pass runs at full depth.

fields.name: Tool Depth
fields.text: Nose cone only: how far the tool is pressed in.

fields.name: Number of Passes
fields.text: Nose cone only: how many times each line is engraved.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Selector... picks vectors by filters so templates find them again.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: Name of the toolpath in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Immediate Output
fields.text: Pick a machine and post processor and save or send this toolpath right away.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the toolpath.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the vectors to engrave.
Pick an engraving tool and set the depth.
Choose Outline or Fill.
Press Calculate, then save it with Immediate Output if you like.

chamferToolpath.summary: Cuts a bevel along the edges of the selected vectors with the cone of a V-bit, or in small steps with a ball nose. Open vectors are cut on the line.

fields.name: Start Depth (D)
fields.text: How far below the material surface the chamfer starts; 0 starts at the top.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: The cutter. Select... picks a V-bit, engraving tool or ball nose; Edit... changes this toolpath's copy.

fields.name: Angle (A)
fields.text: Bevel angle from vertical for a ball nose. With a V-bit it is fixed at half the tool angle.

fields.name: Width (W)
fields.text: How wide the bevel is across the top. Typing it makes the depth follow from the angle.

fields.name: Cut Depth (C)
fields.text: How deep the bevel goes. Typing it makes the width follow from the angle.

fields.name: Overcut
fields.text: Moves the cut out and down the slope so the edge of the cone finishes the foot cleanly.

fields.name: Max Cut Depth
fields.text: Read only: the deepest the chamfer will cut, worked out once a tool is picked.

fields.name: Chamfer Type
fields.text: Inside or Outside: which side of closed vectors gets the bevel.

fields.name: Slope
fields.text: Slope Downwards makes the vector the top edge of the bevel; Slope Upwards makes it the foot.

fields.name: Cut Direction
fields.text: Climb or Conventional milling direction. Climb usually gives a cleaner edge.

fields.name: Use Vector Selection Order
fields.text: Cuts the vectors in the order you selected them instead of an optimized order.

fields.name: Safe Z
fields.text: Read only: the clearance height from Material Setup the tool lifts to between cuts.

fields.name: Home Position
fields.text: Read only: where the tool starts and ends, set in Material Setup.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Manual uses the vectors you select; Selector... sets filters that pick them automatically.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The toolpath's name in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the toolpath from the selected vectors with these settings.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Toolpaths already calculated stay.

steps: Select the vectors whose edges you want to bevel.
Pick a V-bit with Select..., or a ball nose and set the Angle.
Type the Width or the Cut Depth of the bevel.
Choose Inside or Outside and the slope.
Press Calculate.

straightInlayToolpath.summary: Makes straight sided inlays with an end mill: first choose the part to cut, a male insert or a female pocket or hole, and that part's settings open in the panel.

fields.name: Male Inlay (Insert)
fields.text: Straight cuts a plain insert; Stepped cuts an insert with a shoulder step around its edge.

fields.name: Female Inlay (Pocket / Hole)
fields.text: Pocket clears a recess for the insert; Hole cuts right around the inside of the shape.

fields.name: Start Depth (D)
fields.text: How far below the surface the cut starts; usually 0.

fields.name: Cut Depth (C)
fields.text: How deep the insert profile, hole or pocket is cut.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: The end mill used. Select... picks from the Tool Database; the pocket can list several tools.

fields.name: Edit Passes...
fields.text: Shows and changes the depth of each pass; the count is shown beside it.

fields.name: Machine Vectors...
fields.text: Shows the side cut: inserts are cut outside the vectors, holes inside.

fields.name: Direction
fields.text: Climb or Conventional cut direction for the insert or hole.

fields.name: Allowance Offset
fields.text: Extra material trimmed off the insert or hole edge to adjust the fit.

fields.name: Step Depth
fields.text: Stepped insert only: how far down the shoulder step goes. It must end above the cut depth.

fields.name: Step Width
fields.text: Stepped insert only: how wide the shoulder step is.

fields.name: Add tabs to toolpath
fields.text: Leaves small tabs so the insert stays attached; set Length and Thickness, or Edit Tabs...

fields.name: Profile options
fields.text: Pages for ramps, leads, cutting order, start points and sharp corners.

fields.name: Clear Pocket
fields.text: Pocket only: Offset or Raster clearing of the recess.

fields.name: Raster Angle
fields.text: Pocket only, with Raster: the angle of the clearing lines.

fields.name: Profile Pass
fields.text: Pocket only, with Raster: adds a cleanup pass around the edge, first or last.

fields.name: Ramp Plunge Moves
fields.text: Pocket only: ramps into the material over the Distance instead of plunging straight down.

fields.name: Pocket Allowance
fields.text: Pocket only: extra cut round the pocket edge so the insert fits.

fields.name: Use Vector Selection Order
fields.text: Cuts the vectors in the order you selected them.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Manual uses the vectors you select; Selector... picks them with filters.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The toolpath's name in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the inlay toolpath from the selected closed vectors.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Calculated toolpaths stay.

steps: Select the closed vectors of the inlay shape.
Pick the part to make: Straight or Stepped insert, or Pocket or Hole.
Set the depths and pick an end mill.
Adjust the allowance for the fit you want and press Calculate.
Open the form again to make the matching part.

drillBankToolpath.summary: Drills the selected circles with a multi drill head: each firing lowers every drill that lands on a circle of its diameter. Use it on machines with a drill bank, such as boring heads for shelf holes.

fields.name: Start Depth (D)
fields.text: How far below the surface drilling starts; usually 0.

fields.name: Cut Depth (C)
fields.text: How deep each hole is drilled.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: The drill used for feeds and pass depth. Select... picks one; Edit... changes this toolpath's copy.

fields.name: Drill Bank
fields.text: Shows how many drills the bank has, its grid and pitch.

fields.name: Edit Drill Bank...
fields.text: Opens the layout of the bank: drill counts, pitch, reference drill, and each drill's number and diameter.

fields.name: Pitch Tolerance
fields.text: How far circles may be off the bank's pitch and still be drilled in one firing.

fields.name: Diameter Tolerance
fields.text: How far a circle's size may differ from a drill's diameter and still match it.

fields.name: Use Peck Drilling
fields.text: Drills in steps, lifting out between them to clear chips. The peck depth is the tool's pass depth.

fields.name: Retract
fields.text: Where the drill lifts to between pecks: above the start depth, or just above the previous pass.

fields.name: Retract Gap (R)
fields.text: How far above that height the drill lifts between pecks.

fields.name: Dwell at the bottom of each drill pass
fields.text: Pauses the drill at the bottom of each pass for the Dwell Time, in seconds.

fields.name: Project toolpath onto 3D model
fields.text: Measures depths down from the model surface under the tool instead of the flat top.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Manual uses the circles you select; Selector... picks them with filters.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The toolpath's name in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the drill bank toolpath from the selected circles.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Calculated toolpaths stay.

steps: Select the circles to drill.
Press Edit Drill Bank... and set up your drill head to match the machine.
Set the cut depth and pick a drill tool.
Set peck and dwell if needed, then press Calculate.
Save with a post processor that supports a drill bank.

threadMillingToolpath.summary: Mills a screw thread round the center of each selected circle with a thread milling tool, inside a hole or on the outside of a boss.

fields.name: Start Depth (D)
fields.text: How far below the surface the thread starts; usually 0.

fields.name: Max Depth (M)
fields.text: The deepest the cutter goes below the start depth.

fields.name: Thread Length (L)
fields.text: Read only: how long the thread will be, stopping where the lowest tooth reaches.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: The thread mill. Select... picks one; a multi point tool fixes the pitch to its own.

fields.name: Pitch preset
fields.text: Picks a standard thread size to fill in pitch and diameter, or Custom to type them.

fields.name: Pitch (P)
fields.text: Distance between thread crests. Locked when the tool is a multi point cutter.

fields.name: Diameter (D)
fields.text: The major (outer crest) diameter of the thread.

fields.name: Minor Diameter
fields.text: Read only: the root diameter of the thread, worked out from pitch and diameter.

fields.name: Fit Tolerance
fields.text: Cuts a little deeper than the basic thread for an easier fit; start small, such as 0.1 mm.

fields.name: Create Circles for Internal Threads
fields.text: Draws a minor diameter circle at each selected circle, so you can pocket the hole first.

fields.name: Thread Type
fields.text: Internal cuts a thread inside a hole; External cuts it on the outside of a post.

fields.name: Thread Direction
fields.text: Right Handed for normal threads that tighten clockwise, or Left Handed.

fields.name: Top to Bottom
fields.text: Ticked, the tool threads downward from the top; unticked, it cuts upward from the bottom.

fields.name: Use Vector Selection Order
fields.text: Threads the circles in the order you selected them.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Manual uses the circles you select; Selector... picks them with filters.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The toolpath's name in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the thread milling toolpath.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Calculated toolpaths stay.

steps: Select the circles to thread.
Pick a thread milling tool.
Choose a pitch preset or type the pitch and diameter.
For an internal thread, press Create Circles and pocket or drill the holes first.
Set Internal or External and the hand, then press Calculate.

flutingToolpath.summary: Cuts grooves along the selected vectors that sink in and rise out gradually at their ends, for decorative flutes on columns, legs and panels.

fields.name: Start Depth (D)
fields.text: How far below the surface the flute starts; usually 0.

fields.name: Flute Depth
fields.text: The full depth of the flute where it is deepest.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: The cutter, usually a ball nose for round bottomed flutes. Select... picks one.

fields.name: Flute Type
fields.text: Ramp over the whole length, only at the start, or at both start and end.

fields.name: Specify Ramp
fields.text: Set the ramp by a Length or as a Percentage of the vector. Off for a complete ramp.

fields.name: Ramp Length
fields.text: How long each ramp is when set by length.

fields.name: Ramp %
fields.text: How much of each vector's length the ramp takes when set by percentage.

fields.name: Ramp Type
fields.text: Linear ramps at a steady slope; Smooth eases in and out for a softer end.

fields.name: Use Vector Selection Order
fields.text: Cuts the vectors in the order you selected them.

fields.name: Project toolpath onto 3D model
fields.text: Measures depths down from the model surface instead of the flat top.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Manual uses the vectors you select; Selector... picks them with filters.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The toolpath's name in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the fluting toolpath.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Calculated toolpaths stay.

steps: Select the vectors to flute.
Set the flute depth and pick a ball nose tool.
Choose the flute type and ramp length or percentage.
Press Calculate.

prismToolpath.summary: Carves the selected closed vectors into sharp raised prisms with the cone of a V-bit, the ridges following their center lines. Good for beveled lettering and signs.

fields.name: Carve Direction
fields.text: Shown only for older toolpaths: Outside raises the shape as a prism, Inside sinks it as a V channel.

fields.name: Start Depth (D)
fields.text: How far below the surface carving starts; usually 0.

fields.name: Prism Depth
fields.text: Limits how deep the prism is cut. Leave it empty to carve the full prism.

fields.name: Set Depth for Full Prism
fields.text: Fills in the depth the widest selected shape needs to come to a point with this tool.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: The V-bit or engraving tool. Pass depth and stepover come from the tool.

fields.name: Cut Direction
fields.text: Climb or Conventional milling direction.

fields.name: Use Vector Selection Order
fields.text: Carves the vectors in the order you selected them.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Manual uses the vectors you select; Selector... picks them with filters.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The toolpath's name in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the prism toolpath.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Calculated toolpaths stay.

steps: Select the closed vectors to carve.
Pick a V-bit.
Leave Prism Depth empty for full prisms, or type a limit.
Press Calculate. Pocket the waste around the shapes separately if needed.

textureToolpath.summary: Scatters short dipping strokes over the area inside the selected closed vectors for a hand tooled look, or cuts along the selected vectors as the pattern.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: The cutter, usually a ball nose. Select... picks one; Edit... changes this toolpath's copy.

fields.name: Start Depth
fields.text: How far below the surface the strokes start from; usually 0.

fields.name: Use selected vectors as pattern
fields.text: Cuts along the selected vectors instead of scattering random strokes inside them.

fields.name: Ramp at start and end
fields.text: Pattern mode only: each cut dips in and rises out like a flute instead of cutting at full depth.

fields.name: Max. Cut Depth
fields.text: The deepest a stroke cuts below the start depth.

fields.name: Min. Depth
fields.text: Slider: the shallowest stroke as a percent of the max depth, for varied depths.

fields.name: Max. Cut Length
fields.text: The longest a stroke can be.

fields.name: Min Length
fields.text: Slider: the shortest stroke as a percent of the max length.

fields.name: Max Overlap
fields.text: How much a stroke may overlap the one before, as a percent of its length.

fields.name: Variation
fields.text: Overlap slider: 0 always overlaps by the maximum, 100 varies from none up to it.

fields.name: Stepover
fields.text: The distance between rows of strokes.

fields.name: Variation (stepover)
fields.text: Slider: how far strokes may wander across their row, for a less regular look.

fields.name: Angle
fields.text: The direction of the strokes and their rows, in degrees from the X axis.

fields.name: Save ...
fields.text: Saves these texture settings to a file to reuse later.

fields.name: Load ...
fields.text: Loads texture settings saved earlier.

fields.name: Offset
fields.text: Boundary Vector Offset: how far the strokes keep in from the vectors.

fields.name: Project toolpath onto 3D model
fields.text: Measures depths down from the model surface instead of the flat top.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Manual uses the vectors you select; Selector... picks them with filters.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The toolpath's name in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the texture toolpath and shows it.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Calculated toolpaths stay.

steps: Select the closed vectors to texture.
Pick a ball nose tool.
Set the depth, stroke length, stepover and angle.
Adjust the sliders for variety and press Calculate.
Check the result in Preview and tweak until you like it.

materialSetup.summary: Sets the material thickness, where Z zero is, where the model sits inside the material, and the safe heights and home position the machine uses. Heights are measured above the top of the material.

fields.name: Thickness
fields.text: How thick the material is. On a rotary job this field is the Diameter of the stock.

fields.name: Show detailed summary on toolpath tab
fields.text: Shows a fuller material summary at the top of the toolpath panel.

fields.name: Z-Zero
fields.text: Where the tool is zeroed: Material Surface or Machine Bed; on rotary, surface or center of the cylinder.

fields.name: Gap Above Model
fields.text: Pick this to set how much material is left above the 3D model.

fields.name: Gap Below Model
fields.text: Pick this to set the gap between the model's base and the bottom of the material.

fields.name: Model Thickness
fields.text: Read only: the height of the 3D model.

fields.name: Set...
fields.text: Opens Scale Model Z Height to make the model thinner or thicker.

fields.name: Modeling Plane Z
fields.text: Read only: the height of the model's base plane in the material.

fields.name: Clearance (Z1)
fields.text: Height above the material the tool lifts to for rapid moves; clear any clamps.

fields.name: Plunge (Z2)
fields.text: Height above the material where the tool slows to plunge speed. It must not be above Z1.

fields.name: X
fields.text: Home position X, where the tool starts and ends the job.

fields.name: Y
fields.text: Home position Y, where the tool starts and ends the job.

fields.name: Z Gap above Material
fields.text: How high above the material the tool waits at the home position.

fields.name: OK
fields.text: Applies the settings and updates the toolpaths.

fields.name: Cancel
fields.text: Closes the form without changes.

steps: Check the material thickness matches your stock.
Choose whether Z zero is the material surface or the machine bed.
Set the gap above or below the model to position it in the material.
Set Clearance (Z1), Plunge (Z2) and the home position, then press OK.

saveToolpaths.summary: Writes the toolpaths as a file your machine can run. Tick the toolpaths to save and pick the post processor for your machine. A rotary job needs a rotary post: it turns the distance around the blank into the rotary axis in degrees, and the form says which axis. Other posts write the job flat and warn you.

fields.name: Output
fields.text: Save the Selected Toolpath, all visible toolpaths to one file, or visible toolpaths to multiple files.

fields.name: Group where possible
fields.text: With multiple files, neighboring toolpaths cut with one tool share a file.

fields.name: Output Tiled Toolpaths
fields.text: Saves one file per tile. Only available once Toolpath Tiling is set up.

fields.name: Toolpaths to be saved ...
fields.text: Tick the toolpaths to save; each row shows its tool number and tool. Click a row to select it.

fields.name: Machine
fields.text: The machine the files are for; it narrows the post processor list.

fields.name: Post Processor
fields.text: The file format for your machine controller. Add Post-Processors adds more.

fields.name: Output direct to machine
fields.text: Sends the file straight to the machine's control software, when the post supports it.

fields.name: Machine Configuration...
fields.text: Opens the machine settings to add or change machines.

fields.name: Add side to toolpath name
fields.text: Double sided jobs only: adds Top or Bottom to the saved file names.

fields.name: Save Toolpath(s) ...
fields.text: Writes the file or files. It reads Output Toolpath(s) when sending direct.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Show or tick the toolpaths you want to save.
Choose the output: selected toolpath, one file or multiple files.
Pick your machine and its post processor.
Press Save Toolpath(s) ... and choose where to save.
Read any warning shown, such as a post that cannot change tools.

mergeToolpaths.summary: Joins the visible toolpaths that use the same tool into one toolpath, so the machine runs them without a tool change or a trip home between them. The originals are hidden, not deleted.
