fields.name: Toolpaths to be merged ...
fields.text: Lists the visible toolpaths. Show or hide toolpaths in the toolpath list to choose.

fields.name: Ordering
fields.text: Tick Left to Right, Bottom to Top, Grid or Shortest Path; the fastest ticked order is used.

fields.name: Merge By Part
fields.text: Keeps the cuts that lie in one part together before moving on to the next part.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The name of the merged toolpath.

fields.name: Merge Toolpaths
fields.text: Makes the merged toolpath. Each part keeps its own feeds and speed.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Make two or more toolpaths with the same tool visible in the toolpath list.
Tick the orders to try, and Merge By Part if you like.
Type a name and press Merge Toolpaths.

arrayCopyToolpath.summary: Copies the visible toolpaths into a grid of rows and columns to the right of and above them, for cutting several of the same part. The originals are hidden, not deleted.

fields.name: Toolpaths
fields.text: Lists the visible toolpaths that will be copied. Show or hide them in the toolpath list to choose.

fields.name: Rows (Y)
fields.text: How many copies go up the job. Rows times columns must make at least two.

fields.name: Columns (X)
fields.text: How many copies go across the job.

fields.name: Spacing
fields.text: Offset measures from one copy's start to the next; Gap is the space between their outlines.

fields.name: X
fields.text: The spacing across, between columns.

fields.name: Y
fields.text: The spacing up, between rows.

fields.name: Minimize tool changes
fields.text: When the toolpaths use different tools, cuts all copies with one tool before changing.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The name of the new array toolpath.

fields.name: Create
fields.text: Makes the array copy. Recalculating a copy follows the original toolpaths.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Make only the toolpaths to copy visible in the toolpath list.
Set the number of rows and columns.
Choose Offset or Gap and type the X and Y spacing.
Press Create.

toolpathTiling.summary: Splits the toolpaths of a job bigger than your machine into tiles that are cut one after another, moving the material on by one tile between them. The XY datum must be at the bottom left of the job.

fields.name: Tile Toolpaths
fields.text: Turns tiling on. It needs the XY datum at the bottom left corner, set in Job Setup.

fields.name: Tiling Method
fields.text: Individual Tiles for separate pieces, or Feed-through in X or Y for one board moved along the machine.

fields.name: Tile Width (x)
fields.text: How wide each tile is; set it to what your machine can cut. Hidden for Feed-through in Y.

fields.name: Tile Height (y)
fields.text: How tall each tile is. Hidden for Feed-through in X.

fields.name: Tile Overlap
fields.text: How far tiles overlap. For individual tiles use at least the tool radius; it must be smaller than the tile.

fields.name: Machine smallest tile first
fields.text: Cuts the smallest tile before the others.

fields.name: Update Tiles
fields.text: Works out the tiles with these settings and draws them.

fields.name: Active Tile
fields.text: Picks which tile the view and preview show; the count of tiles is shown above.

fields.name: Draw toolpaths in original position for visualization
fields.text: Draws the tiled toolpaths where they sit in the full job instead of at the datum.

fields.name: Delete All Tiling Data
fields.text: Removes the tiles so the toolpaths are drawn and saved whole again.

fields.name: Hide Tiling Manager
fields.text: Closes the form. The tiling settings stay.

steps: Make sure the XY datum is at the bottom left in Job Setup.
Tick Tile Toolpaths and choose a tiling method.
Type the tile size and overlap, then press Update Tiles.
Save the toolpaths with Output Tiled Toolpaths ticked to get one file per tile.

photoCarveToolpath.summary: Carves a photograph as V grooves across the selected bitmap, cutting deeper and wider where the picture is darker. Select the bitmap, and vectors if you want the grooves to follow them.

fields.name: Start Depth (D)
fields.text: How far below the surface carving starts; usually 0.

fields.name: Max Carving Depth
fields.text: How deep the grooves go in the darkest parts of the picture.

fields.name: Stepover Retract
fields.text: How high the tool lifts when moving from one groove to the next.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: The V-bit that carves the grooves. Select... picks one.

fields.name: Strategy
fields.text: Raster uses parallel lines, Hatch uses crossing lines, Selected Vectors follows your vectors.

fields.name: Line Spacing
fields.text: Slider from Dense to Sparse: percent of the groove width; 100 leaves a sharp ridge between grooves.

fields.name: Line Angle
fields.text: The angle of the groove lines, from -90 to 90 degrees. Off with Selected Vectors.

fields.name: Project toolpath onto 3D model
fields.text: Measures depths down from the model surface instead of the flat top.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The toolpath's name in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the photo carving toolpath. It needs a selected bitmap and a tool.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Calculated toolpaths stay.

steps: Select the bitmap to carve, and any vectors to follow.
Pick a V-bit and set the max carving depth.
Choose a strategy, line spacing and angle.
Press Calculate, then check the result in Preview.

importedToolpath.summary: Edits a toolpath read from a G-code file: place it in the job, set how deep it cuts and its feeds. Imported moves are never recalculated.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The toolpath's name in the toolpath list; it cannot be empty.

fields.name: Move X
fields.text: Shifts the whole toolpath left or right by this distance.

fields.name: Move Y
fields.text: Shifts the whole toolpath up or down by this distance.

fields.name: Start Depth (D)
fields.text: Lowers the toolpath by this much below the surface.

fields.name: Feed Rate
fields.text: Cutting speed of the tool across the material.

fields.name: Plunge Rate
fields.text: Speed the tool moves down into the material.

fields.name: Spindle Speed
fields.text: Spindle speed in r.p.m. written with the toolpath.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: The tool the preview draws with. Select... picks one from the Tool Database.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Saves these changes to the imported toolpath.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Import the G-code file, or open an imported toolpath from the list.
Move it into place with Move X and Move Y.
Set the start depth, feeds and a tool for the preview.
Press Apply.

previewToolpaths.summary: Shows the material being cut by your toolpaths in the 3D view, with an estimated machining time, and checks the result for gouges, collisions and leftover material before you cut.

fields.name: Material Appearance...
fields.text: Picks the wood or material look and color the preview uses.

fields.name: Machined Area Color ....
fields.text: How cut areas are shaded: Material Color, Surface Color, Global Fill Color, Toolpath Color or Lithophane.

fields.name: Set All
fields.text: Toolpath Color only: gives every toolpath the fill color of the selected one.

fields.name: No fill
fields.text: Toolpath Color only: the selected toolpath's cuts show in the material color.

fields.name: Light fall off
fields.text: Lithophane only: how quickly light fades through thicker material.

fields.name: Animate preview
fields.text: Shows the cutting move by move instead of all at once.

fields.name: Draw tool
fields.text: Shows the tool moving during an animated preview.

fields.name: Preview Selected Toolpath
fields.text: Cuts only the toolpath selected in the list.

fields.name: Playback
fields.text: Run, Pause, Single Step and Run to Retract control an animated preview.

fields.name: Speed
fields.text: How fast the animated preview plays.

fields.name: Preview All Sides
fields.text: Double sided jobs: cuts the visible toolpaths of both sides.

fields.name: Preview All Toolpaths
fields.text: Cuts every toolpath in the list, visible or not.

fields.name: Preview Visible Toolpaths
fields.text: Cuts only the toolpaths shown in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Reset Preview
fields.text: Puts the material back to uncut.

fields.name: Undo Last
fields.text: Takes back the last preview or waste removal.

fields.name: Save Preview Image...
fields.text: Saves a picture of the 3D preview to a file.

fields.name: Show Check Colors
fields.text: Paints gouges red, leftover material blue and undercuts violet, and lists each issue.

fields.name: Tolerance
fields.text: How far the preview may differ from the design before a check flags it.

fields.name: Issues found by the preview
fields.text: Each issue with its toolpath and position; click one to show it in the 3D view.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Show the toolpaths you want in the toolpath list.
Press Preview Visible Toolpaths, or tick Animate preview first to watch it cut.
Double click waste areas in the 3D view to remove them.
Turn on check colors and review any issues listed.
Press Reset Preview before trying again.

createFlatShape.summary: Makes a flat plane component from the selected closed vectors, lifted by its base height. With nothing selected the plane covers the whole material.

fields.name: Base Height
fields.text: Lifts the whole shape by this amount; 0 starts it at the modeling plane.

fields.name: Fade
fields.text: Makes the component fade in height between two anchor points; Set Anchor picks them in the 3D view.

fields.name: Fade by
fields.text: Percent of the height taken away at the second anchor; 50 halves it.

fields.name: Tilt
fields.text: Tilts the component up from one anchor point toward another; Set Anchor picks them.

fields.name: Tilt Angle
fields.text: How far it tilts, in degrees, between -90 and 90.

fields.name: Component Name
fields.text: The name of the component in the component tree.

fields.name: Combine
fields.text: How it joins the model: Add stacks on top, Subtract cuts into it, Merge keeps the higher.

fields.name: Reset
fields.text: Discards what this form applied, putting the model back as it was when the form opened.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Makes the component, or updates the one this form made last.

fields.name: Start New Component
fields.text: Keeps what is applied and clears the selection, so the next Apply makes a new component.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Applied components stay.

steps: Select the closed vectors, or nothing to cover the whole material.
Type the Base Height of the plane.
Pick how it combines with the model.
Press Apply and check the 3D view.

importModel.summary: Brings a 3D model file into the job: choose which face looks up, turn it, and set its size before positioning it. The 3D view shows the result as you go.

fields.name: Choose File...
fields.text: Picks the 3D model file to import; its name and triangle count are shown.

fields.name: Imported model type
fields.text: Rotary jobs only: Full 3D model wraps around the axis; Flat model imports as for a flat job.

fields.name: Face on top
fields.text: Which face of the model points up: Top, Bottom, Front, Back, Left or Right.

fields.name: Rotate about Z
fields.text: Buttons that turn the model by 90, 180 or 45 degrees about the vertical axis.

fields.name: About X
fields.text: Turns the model about the X axis by the typed angle. You can also drag the rings.

fields.name: About Y
fields.text: Turns the model about the Y axis by the angle typed.

fields.name: About Z
fields.text: Turns the model about the Z axis by the angle typed.

fields.name: Reset Rotation
fields.text: Sets all three rotation angles back to 0.

fields.name: X
fields.text: Model Size: the model's width.

fields.name: Y
fields.text: Model Size: the model's depth from front to back.

fields.name: Z
fields.text: Model Size: the model's height.

fields.name: Lock XYZ Ratio
fields.text: Keeps the proportions when you change one size.

fields.name: Units
fields.text: Whether the file's numbers are mm or inches.

fields.name: Scale x 25.4 (inches to mm)
fields.text: Makes the model 25.4 times bigger, for a file drawn in inches.

fields.name: Scale ÷ 25.4 (mm to inches)
fields.text: Makes the model 25.4 times smaller, for a file drawn in mm.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Applies the sizes typed above.

fields.name: Center Model
fields.text: Moves the model back to the middle of the rotation handles.

fields.name: Apply Perspective along Z
fields.text: Shrinks the far parts of the model for a perspective look; the slider sets the amount.

fields.name: Model units
fields.text: Rotary full model only: the units of the file.

fields.name: Rotation Axis Movement
fields.text: Rotary full model only: On lets you drag the rotation axis within the model.

fields.name: Model Scaling
fields.text: Rotary full model only: set Length and Diameter, fit to the material, or reset or resize the material.

fields.name: Position & Import
fields.text: Goes on to place the model in the material and import it.

fields.name: Segment
fields.text: Goes on to cut the model into pieces that each carve from above.

fields.name: Cancel
fields.text: Closes the form without importing.

steps: Press Choose File... and pick the model.
Choose the face on top and turn the model until it looks right.
Set the size and units, then press Apply.
Press Position & Import to place it, or Segment to split it first.

positionModel.summary: Sets where an imported 3D model is cut off before it becomes a component. Everything above the zero plane becomes the component; undercuts become straight walls down.

fields.name: Zero Plane Position
fields.text: Slider and box: the height above the model's lowest point where it is cut off.

fields.name: Middle
fields.text: Puts the zero plane halfway up the model.

fields.name: Bottom
fields.text: Puts the zero plane at the model's lowest point, keeping all of it.

fields.name: Create Both Sides
fields.text: Double sided jobs only: also makes a component on the other side from what lies below the plane.

fields.name: Discard data below zero plane
fields.text: Drops everything below the plane. Unticked, those parts stay as depths below zero.

fields.name: Highlight Undercuts
fields.text: Colors areas the tool cannot reach from above, so you can adjust the orientation.

fields.name: Back
fields.text: Returns to the orientation step.

fields.name: Import
fields.text: Makes the component and adds it to the model.

fields.name: Cancel
fields.text: Stops the import without adding anything.

steps: Drag the slider or type where the model should be cut off.
Tick Highlight Undercuts to check for areas the tool cannot reach.
Press Back to change the orientation if needed.
Press Import.

segmentModel.summary: Cuts an imported 3D model into segments that can each be carved from above, then lays them out flat in the material. Use it for models with undercuts that one side cannot reach.

fields.name: Mode
fields.text: Edit places segmenting planes and cuts; Layout turns each segment to face up.

fields.name: X
fields.text: Edit mode: moves the segmenting plane along X. You can also drag its handles in the 3D view.

fields.name: Y
fields.text: Edit mode: moves the segmenting plane along Y.

fields.name: Z
fields.text: Edit mode: moves the segmenting plane up or down.

fields.name: Tilt about X
fields.text: Edit mode: tilts the plane about the X axis, in degrees.

fields.name: Tilt about Y
fields.text: Edit mode: tilts the plane about the Y axis, in degrees.

fields.name: Segment
fields.text: Edit mode: cuts the selected segment in two along the plane.

fields.name: Segments
fields.text: The tree of segments. Drag one onto another to merge them; right click for Delete Children or Separate.

fields.name: Segment Orientation
fields.text: Layout mode: Turn up, down, left, right or Rotate flat turns the selected segment.

fields.name: Free Rotation
fields.text: Layout mode: shows About X, Y and Z fields to turn the segment by any angle.

fields.name: Visualize Undercuts
fields.text: Layout mode: colors areas of the segment the tool cannot reach from above.

fields.name: Create Backface Caps
fields.text: Fills the cut faces of each segment flat.

fields.name: Resize Material To Fit Slices
fields.text: Grows the material so it holds all the laid out segments.

fields.name: Create Boundary Vectors
fields.text: Draws each segment's top and bottom outlines as vectors.

fields.name: Back
fields.text: Returns to the orientation step.

fields.name: OK
fields.text: Makes the segments as components laid out in the material.

fields.name: Cancel
fields.text: Stops the import without adding anything.

steps: In Edit mode, place the plane where the model should split and press Segment.
Repeat on other segments until each can be carved from above.
Switch to Layout and turn each segment so it faces up.
Tick the options you want and press OK.

twoRailSweep.summary: Sweeps one or more cross section vectors along two drive rails into a component; the section stretches to fill the gap between the rails. Good for frames, legs and tapered moldings.

fields.name: Use Selection
fields.text: Takes the two selected vectors as the rails; the first shows red, the second green.

fields.name: Swap Rail Order
fields.text: Swaps which rail is first and which is second.

fields.name: Clear Rails
fields.text: Forgets the chosen rails so you can pick others.

fields.name: Cross Sections
fields.text: Select an open vector and click a rail to attach it; right click rails or sections for more options.

fields.name: Scale cross sections with width
fields.text: Makes the section taller where the rails are farther apart. Unticked, heights stay as drawn.

fields.name: Sweep between spans
fields.text: Blends sections with the same number of spans span by span, for crisper transitions.

fields.name: Fill center of inner closed vector rails
fields.text: With two closed rails, fills inside the inner one at the height the sections reach.

fields.name: Scale to Exact Height
fields.text: Scales the sweep so its highest point is the Height typed.

fields.name: Height
fields.text: The top height used with Scale to Exact Height.

fields.name: Component Name
fields.text: The name of the component in the component tree.

fields.name: Combine
fields.text: How it joins the model: Add stacks on top, Subtract cuts into it, Merge keeps the higher.

fields.name: Reset
fields.text: Discards what this form applied, putting the model back as it was when the form opened.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Makes the component, or updates the one this form made last.

fields.name: Start New Component
fields.text: Keeps what is applied and clears the selection, so the next Apply makes a new component.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Applied components stay.

steps: Select the two rail vectors and press Use Selection.
Select an open cross section vector and click a rail to attach it; add more if you like.
Set the height options.
Press Apply and check the 3D view.

extrudeWeave.summary: Extrudes cross section vectors, or a component, along one or more drive rails into a new component. Where rails cross, the strands can weave over and under each other.

fields.name: Use Selection
fields.text: Takes the selected vectors as the drive rails; each shows its start and direction.

fields.name: Clear Rails
fields.text: Forgets the chosen rails so you can pick others.

fields.name: Extrude
fields.text: Use Vector Cross Sections to sweep open vectors, or Use a Component to run a component along the rail.

fields.name: Cross Sections / Sweep Interior
fields.text: Select an open vector and click a rail to attach it; drag it along the rail, right click for more.

fields.name: Create sharp corners
fields.text: Miters the corners of the rails instead of rounding them.

fields.name: Sweep between spans
fields.text: Blends sections with the same number of spans span by span.

fields.name: Component
fields.text: With a component: the component to run along the rail, its X following the rail.

fields.name: Along the rail
fields.text: Stretch one copy to the rail's length, or fill the rail with multiple copies.

fields.name: Overlap
fields.text: With copies: how much of its length each copy overlaps the one before, in percent.

fields.name: Flip alternate copies
fields.text: With copies: flips every other copy across the rail.

fields.name: Weave under/over at crossings
fields.text: Raises and lowers the strands where rails cross, alternately over and under.

fields.name: Weave
fields.text: Scale Shape scales the heights at crossings; Add Base keeps them and lifts by the percentages.

fields.name: Z Under
fields.text: Height, in percent, of a strand where it passes under another.

fields.name: Z Over
fields.text: Height, in percent, of a strand where it passes over another; it can be above 100.

fields.name: Scale to Exact Height
fields.text: Scales the result so its highest point is the Height typed.

fields.name: Height
fields.text: The top height used with Scale to Exact Height.

fields.name: Component Name
fields.text: The name of the component in the component tree.

fields.name: Combine
fields.text: How it joins the model: Add stacks on top, Subtract cuts into it, Merge keeps the higher.

fields.name: Reset
fields.text: Discards what this form applied, putting the model back as it was when the form opened.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Makes the component, or updates the one this form made last.

fields.name: Start New Component
fields.text: Keeps what is applied and clears the selection, so the next Apply makes a new component.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Applied components stay.

steps: Select the rail vectors and press Use Selection.
Choose vector cross sections or a component.
Attach a cross section to a rail, or pick the component.
Tick Weave if the rails cross, then press Apply.

textureArea.summary: Fills an area with repeating copies of a component to make a relief texture. Select the component to repeat and, to limit the area, closed vectors around it; the original is hidden.

fields.name: Mode
fields.text: Transform Object moves the result; Edit Textured Area Component lets you drag the tile box in 2D.

fields.name: X
fields.text: Spacing: gap between tiles across, as a percent of the tile width; below zero overlaps them.

fields.name: Y
fields.text: Spacing: gap between tiles upward, as a percent of the tile height.

fields.name: X Shift
fields.text: Moves every other row across by this percent of the tile width, for a brick pattern.

fields.name: Y Shift
fields.text: Moves every other column up by this percent of the tile height.

fields.name: Reflection
fields.text: Click each of the four tiles to cycle it through no, horizontal, vertical or both reflections.

fields.name: Component Name
fields.text: The name of the component in the component tree.

fields.name: Combine
fields.text: How it joins the model: Add stacks on top, Subtract cuts into it, Merge keeps the higher.

fields.name: Reset
fields.text: Discards what this form applied, putting the model back as it was when the form opened.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Makes the component, or updates the one this form made last.

fields.name: Start New Component
fields.text: Keeps what is applied and clears the selection, so the next Apply makes a new component.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Applied components stay.

steps: Select the component to repeat.
Also select closed vectors to limit the area, or none to fill the job.
Set the spacing, shifts and reflections.
Press Apply and check the 3D view.

fields.name: Mode
fields.text: Turn spins the profile around the line joining its ends, like a lathe; Spin turns it around its left end.

fields.name: Scale to Exact Height
fields.text: Scales the result so its highest point is the Height typed.

fields.name: Height
fields.text: The top height used with Scale to Exact Height.

fields.name: Component Name
fields.text: The name of the component in the component tree.

fields.name: Combine
fields.text: How it joins the model: Add stacks on top, Subtract cuts into it, Merge keeps the higher.

fields.name: Reset
fields.text: Discards what this form applied, putting the model back as it was when the form opened.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Makes the component, or updates the one this form made last.

fields.name: Start New Component
fields.text: Keeps what is applied and clears the selection, so the next Apply makes a new component.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Applied components stay.

steps: Draw an open vector for the profile.
Select it and choose Turn or Spin.
For Spin, move the vector right so the round shape has room.
Press Apply and check the 3D view.

componentEdit.summary: Changes the component selected in the component list with one edit at a time: smooth, draft, tilt, fade, mirror, flip, scale heights or emboss. Each edit is one undo step.

fields.name: Edit
fields.text: Picks the change to make; the fields below change to suit it.

fields.name: Strength
fields.text: Smooth: blur radius; each pass averages heights within this distance. Larger is softer.

fields.name: Passes
fields.text: Smooth: how many times the blur is repeated.

fields.name: Draft Angle
fields.text: Add Draft: how far the walls slope outward, in degrees, so the shape cuts from above.

fields.name: Tilt Angle
fields.text: Tilt: how steeply the component rises toward one side, in degrees.

fields.name: Direction
fields.text: Tilt or Fade: the direction of the slope or fade, in degrees counterclockwise from X.

fields.name: Pivot at the component center
fields.text: Tilt: pivots about the component's center; untick to type Pivot X and Pivot Y.

fields.name: Fade Start
fields.text: Fade: where the fade begins, as a percent across the component; heights are full before it.

fields.name: Fade End
fields.text: Fade: where heights reach zero, as a percent; it must be after the start.

fields.name: Mirror
fields.text: Mirror: flips the component left to right or top to bottom about its own center.

fields.name: Scale Factor
fields.text: Scale Heights: multiplies every height; 0.5 halves them.

fields.name: Base Offset
fields.text: Scale Heights: adds this amount to every height after scaling.

fields.name: Maximum Height
fields.text: Emboss: squashes heights so the top is at this height, keeping the detail.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Makes the chosen edit to the selected component.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Edits made stay.

steps: Select a component in the component list.
Choose the edit to make.
Fill in its settings.
Press Apply; use Undo to take it back.

componentProperties.summary: Shows and changes the properties of the component, group or level picked in the Component Tree. Changes apply as soon as you stop typing; with several components picked, they apply to all.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The name shown in the Component Tree; it cannot be empty. Hidden when several components are picked.

fields.name: Combine Mode
fields.text: How it joins what is below it: Add, Subtract, Merge, Low or Multiply.

fields.name: Shape Height
fields.text: Components: scales the component's heights, as a percent; 100 keeps them as made.

fields.name: Base Height
fields.text: Lifts the component or level by this amount.

fields.name: Fade
fields.text: Components: fades the height between two anchor points picked with Set Anchor.

fields.name: Fade by
fields.text: Percent of the height taken away at the second fade anchor.

fields.name: Tilt
fields.text: Components: tilts the component up from one anchor toward another.

fields.name: Tilt Angle
fields.text: How far the component tilts, in degrees.

fields.name: Bake
fields.text: Makes the shape height, base height, fade and tilt a permanent part of the component.

fields.name: Appearance
fields.text: How it is colored in the 3D view: from its parent or children, a solid color, or a material.

fields.name: Color swatch
fields.text: The color used when Appearance is Solid Color.

fields.name: Material
fields.text: The material look used when Appearance is Use Material, such as Oak or MDF.

fields.name: Highlight Selected Component
fields.text: Highlights the picked components in the 3D view while the form is open.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Applies any change still waiting and closes the form.

steps: Pick a component, group or level in the Component Tree.
Change its name, combine mode or heights.
Set its appearance in the 3D view.
Press Bake to fix fade and tilt for good, if you want.

componentTransform.summary: Moves, scales and rotates the selected component flat in XY by the amounts you type. Heights are not scaled, and the change is one undo step.

fields.name: Move X
fields.text: Moves the component left or right by this distance.

fields.name: Move Y
fields.text: Moves the component up or down by this distance.

fields.name: Scale X
fields.text: Stretches the component's width, as a percent; 100 keeps it the same.

fields.name: Scale Y
fields.text: Stretches the component's depth, as a percent.

fields.name: Link X and Y
fields.text: Keeps Scale X and Scale Y the same so the shape keeps its proportions.

fields.name: Angle
fields.text: Rotates the component, in degrees; positive angles turn counterclockwise.

fields.name: Pivot
fields.text: Scales and rotates about the Component center, or about a Point you type as Pivot X and Pivot Y.

fields.name: Reset
fields.text: Puts every field back to no change.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Moves, scales and rotates the selected component.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select a component in the component list.
Type the move, scale and angle you want.
Choose the pivot and press Apply.

exportStl.summary: Turns the whole model, or the selected component, into a triangle mesh and saves it as an STL, OBJ or POV-Ray file for 3D printing or other programs.

fields.name: Limit Triangles By...
fields.text: Limits the mesh by an approximate tolerance or by a maximum number of triangles.

fields.name: Tolerance
fields.text: How far the mesh may stray from the model; smaller keeps more detail and makes a bigger file.

fields.name: Triangles
fields.text: The most triangles the mesh may have; more keeps more detail.

fields.name: Back face of triangulation
fields.text: How the back is closed: left open, mirrored, a flat plane, the other side, or sides on rotary.

fields.name: Triangulate
fields.text: Builds the mesh and shows it in the 3D view before you save.

fields.name: Num Tri Created
fields.text: Read only: how many triangles the mesh has.

fields.name: Maximum Error
fields.text: Read only: the largest distance between the mesh and the model.

fields.name: Draw shaded triangulation
fields.text: Shows the mesh shaded; untick to see it as a wireframe.

fields.name: Save Triangulation...
fields.text: Saves the mesh; the file type you choose sets STL, OBJ or POV-Ray.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select a component to export only it, or nothing for the whole model.
Set the tolerance or triangle count.
Choose how to close the back; a flat plane suits 3D printing.
Press Triangulate to check the mesh, then Save Triangulation...

replaceBelow.summary: Trims or flattens the bottom of the selected components below a height. Several components, or a level, are baked into one component first.

fields.name: Replace Value Below
fields.text: The cut off height, measured on the chosen components. You can also drag the blue pin in the 3D view.

fields.name: Replace Value With
fields.text: Transparent removes everything below the height; Plane raises it flat to that height.

fields.name: Lower Component by Value
fields.text: Afterward drops what is left by the same height so it sits back at zero.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Trims or flattens the component.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Select the components, or make a level active.
Type the height or drag the blue pin in the 3D view.
Choose Transparent or Plane, and whether to lower the result.
Press Apply.

crossSection.summary: Draws the model's height along a line as an open vector, so you can see or reuse its profile. The vector goes on the active layer just above the top left of the job, distance along X and height along Y.

fields.name: Start point
fields.text: Click in the 2D view where the section line starts.

fields.name: End point
fields.text: Click where the line ends; the profile vector is drawn straight away.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Vectors already drawn stay.

steps: Open the form and click the start of the line across the model in the 2D view.
Click the end of the line.
Find the new profile vector above the top left of the job.

sliceModel.summary: Cuts a model that is thicker than your material into Z slices that can be machined from separate boards and glued together. Each slice becomes a component dropped to the zero plane; the originals are hidden.

fields.name: Model Thickness
fields.text: Read only: the height of the model being sliced.

fields.name: Material Thickness
fields.text: Read only: the job's material thickness, a good slice thickness to aim for.

fields.name: Slice by
fields.text: Slice Thickness makes slices of a set thickness; Number of Slices divides the height equally.

fields.name: Slice Thickness
fields.text: How thick each slice is, usually your board thickness.

fields.name: From Top
fields.text: Slices from the top down, leaving the thinner part slice at the bottom. Off, it is at the top.

fields.name: Number of Slices
fields.text: Divides the model height into this many equal slices.

fields.name: Create Boundary Vectors
fields.text: Outlines each slice with vectors on a new layer named after the slice.

fields.name: Height bar
fields.text: Shows the cut heights; double click it to add a height there.

fields.name: Slice heights
fields.text: Lists the Z heights the model is cut at. Pick one to edit it, or New height to add one.

fields.name: Z height
fields.text: The height of the picked slice line; type a new value and press Apply.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Saves the typed Z height to the list.

fields.name: Delete
fields.text: Removes the picked height from the list.

fields.name: Slice Model
fields.text: Cuts the model into slice components. It is one undo step.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Check the model and material thickness.
Choose to slice by thickness or by number of slices.
Adjust individual heights in the list or on the bar if needed.
Press Slice Model, then make toolpaths for each slice.

smoothComponents.summary: Smooths the whole selected component to soften detail and edges. The 3D view shows the result as you move the slider.

fields.name: Smoothing
fields.text: Slider from 0 to 100 percent: how strongly the component is smoothed. Release it to see the result.

fields.name: Preserve Transparency
fields.text: Keeps the smoothing inside the component so its outline does not blur into the background.

fields.name: Bake Current Smoothing
fields.text: Fixes the current smoothing in place; move the slider again to smooth further.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form, keeping the smoothing shown.

steps: Select a component in the Components list.
Move the Smoothing slider and watch the 3D view.
Press Bake Current Smoothing to lock it in, and smooth again if needed.

embossComponent.summary: Lowers the selected component while keeping its fine detail, for turning a full 3D model into a low relief. The 3D view previews each change.

fields.name: Scale Height
fields.text: Slider from 1 to 100 percent: how tall the embossed component is compared to now.

fields.name: Height
fields.text: Read only: the component's height at the current scale.

fields.name: Detail Smoothness
fields.text: Slider: how much the kept detail is smoothed. Lower heights need more smoothing.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Keeps the embossed component.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form and takes back the preview if you did not apply it.

steps: Select a full 3D component in the Components list.
Lower the Scale Height slider to the relief height you want.
Adjust Detail Smoothness until the detail looks clean.
Press Apply.

scaleModelHeight.summary: Scales the height of the whole model up or down. Every component keeps its shape; only its height scale changes. The 3D view previews the change.

fields.name: Model height
fields.text: Read only: the current height of the model.

fields.name: Scale Both Sides
fields.text: Double sided jobs only: scales the model on both sides together.

fields.name: Scale Height
fields.text: Slider: scales the model height by a percent; release it to preview.

fields.name: Height
fields.text: Set Exact Height: type the height the model's top should reach.

fields.name: Set Height
fields.text: Previews the model scaled to the typed height.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Keeps the new model height.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form and takes back the preview if you did not apply it.

steps: Open the form; the current model height is shown.
Move the slider, or type a height and press Set Height.
Check the 3D view and press Apply.

offsetModel.summary: Grows or shrinks the visible model in 3D by a distance. The result becomes one new component; the original components stay in the tree, hidden.

fields.name: Offset Distance
fields.text: How far to offset the surface: positive grows the model, negative shrinks it. It cannot be zero.

fields.name: Clip Z values to the Zero Plane
fields.text: Stops the result dropping below the zero plane, so flat areas stay where they are.

fields.name: Preview
fields.text: Shows the offset result; each Preview offsets the result again.

fields.name: OK
fields.text: Keeps the offset model as a new component.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form and takes back any previews.

steps: Show the components you want to offset.
Type the offset distance.
Press Preview to check it in the 3D view.
Press OK to keep it.

addDraft.summary: Makes a new component from the visible model with no wall steeper than the draft angle, useful for molds and vacuum forming. The original components stay visible under it.

fields.name: Draft Angle
fields.text: Slider and box: wall angle from vertical, above 0 and below 90 degrees; larger angles slope the walls more.

fields.name: Apply
fields.text: Makes the drafted component from the visible model.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form.

steps: Show the components that make up the model.
Set the draft angle.
Press Apply and check the new component in the 3D view.

rough3dToolpath.summary: Clears the bulk of the material above the 3D model, level by level, leaving an allowance for the finishing pass. Use a large end mill before a 3D finish toolpath.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: The roughing cutter, usually a large end mill. Select... picks one; Edit... changes this copy.

fields.name: Machining Limit Boundary
fields.text: Where to cut: Model Boundary, Material Boundary, Selected Vector(s) or a Selected Level.

fields.name: Level
fields.text: With Selected Level: the model level whose components limit the toolpath.

fields.name: Boundary Offset
fields.text: Grows the boundary outward by this much; a negative value shrinks it.

fields.name: Machining Allowance
fields.text: Material left on the model for the finish pass; a small amount such as 0.5 mm.

fields.name: Strategy
fields.text: Z Level clears flat layers with raster lines; 3D Raster follows the surface in passes.

fields.name: Profile
fields.text: Z Level only: cut round the outline of each level First, Last or not at all.

fields.name: Order
fields.text: Z Level only: Level by level clears whole levels; Depth first takes each area to the bottom.

fields.name: Raster Direction
fields.text: Whether the raster lines run Along X or Along Y.

fields.name: Reverse step direction
fields.text: Z Level only: raster lines start at the far edge instead.

fields.name: Avoid machined areas
fields.text: 3D Raster only: skips what an earlier level already cut to the allowance.

fields.name: Ramp plunge moves
fields.text: Z Level only: ramps into the material over the Distance instead of plunging straight down.

fields.name: Distance
fields.text: How long each ramp is.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Manual uses the vectors you select; Selector... picks them with filters.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The toolpath's name in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the toolpath. It needs a 3D model, and vectors or a level if chosen as boundary.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Calculated toolpaths stay.

steps: Build the 3D model first.
Pick a large end mill.
Choose the boundary and machining allowance.
Pick a strategy and press Calculate.
Follow it with a 3D finish toolpath.

finish3dToolpath.summary: Follows the 3D model surface with raster passes or offset rings for a smooth finish. Add smaller tools to finish detail the first tool cannot reach.

fields.name: Tools
fields.text: The finishing tools, usually ball noses. The first cuts everything; later ones finish what earlier ones missed.

fields.name: Machining Limit Boundary
fields.text: Where to cut: Model Boundary, Material Boundary, Selected Vector(s) or a Selected Level.

fields.name: Level
fields.text: With Selected Level: the model level whose components limit the toolpath.

fields.name: Boundary Offset
fields.text: Grows the boundary outward by this much; a negative value shrinks it.

fields.name: Minimum Detail
fields.text: Slider from Coarse to Fine: material thinner than this is not worth another tool. Needs two or more tools.

fields.name: Rest Boundary Offset
fields.text: How far each area left for a later tool is grown, so its cuts blend in.

fields.name: Strategy
fields.text: Offset follows rings around the model; Raster runs parallel lines across it.

fields.name: Cut Direction
fields.text: Offset only: Climb or Conventional.

fields.name: Raster Angle
fields.text: Raster only: the angle of the lines in degrees; 0 runs along X.

fields.name: Stepover Retract
fields.text: Offset only: how far the tool lifts between rings; 0 stays on the surface.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Manual uses the vectors you select; Selector... picks them with filters.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The toolpath's name in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the toolpath. It needs a 3D model, and vectors or a level if chosen as boundary.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Calculated toolpaths stay.

steps: Rough the model first with a 3D roughing toolpath.
Pick a ball nose, and add smaller tools for fine detail if needed.
Choose the boundary and strategy.
Press Calculate and check it in Preview.

laserCutFillToolpath.summary: Burns along the selected vectors with a laser, fills closed shapes with hatch lines, or both. Use it to cut out parts or engrave filled areas.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: The laser tool. Select... picks one from the Tool Database; it must be a laser.

fields.name: Power
fields.text: Laser power in percent. Leave empty to use the tool's setting.

fields.name: Move Speed
fields.text: How fast the laser moves while burning. Leave empty to use the tool's setting.

fields.name: Cut Depth
fields.text: How deep to cut; deeper cuts step down in passes of the laser's pass depth. 0 burns at the surface.

fields.name: No. Passes
fields.text: Read only: how many depth passes the cut depth needs.

fields.name: No. Repeats
fields.text: How many times each pass is burned.

fields.name: Overscan
fields.text: Hatch fill only: runs each fill line a little past the shape, as a percent, for even burning.

fields.name: Strategy
fields.text: Cut Outside, Cut Inside or Cut On the vectors, or Hatch Fill closed shapes.

fields.name: Allowance
fields.text: Outside or inside cuts: extra offset beyond the laser's kerf.

fields.name: Stepover
fields.text: Hatch fill: the distance between fill lines.

fields.name: Hatch Angle
fields.text: Hatch fill: the angle of the fill lines, in degrees.

fields.name: Fill
fields.text: Fill Together treats all shapes as one area; Fill Regionally fills each area on its own.

fields.name: Cross Hatch
fields.text: Hatch fill: adds a second set of lines across the first.

fields.name: Outline
fields.text: Hatch fill: also burns around the outline of each shape.

fields.name: Project toolpath onto 3D model
fields.text: Follows the model surface instead of the flat top.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Manual uses the vectors you select; Selector... picks them with filters.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The toolpath's name in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the laser toolpath. It needs a laser tool and selected vectors.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Calculated toolpaths stay.

fields.name: Immediate Output
fields.text: Machine, Post Processor and Save Toolpath(s) ... save this toolpath right after calculating it.

steps: Select the vectors to cut or fill.
Pick a laser tool and set power and speed.
Choose the strategy, and hatch settings for a fill.
Press Calculate, then save it for your laser.

sketchToolpath.summary: Finds the key lines of a bitmap or of the 3D model and carves them with a V-bit or ball nose, like a pencil sketch.

fields.name: Selection
fields.text: Sketch a Bitmap selected in the 2D view, or the 3D Model.

fields.name: Left (X)
fields.text: Older toolpaths that read an image file only: the left edge of the picture.

fields.name: Bottom (Y)
fields.text: Older toolpaths only: the bottom edge of the picture.

fields.name: Width
fields.text: Older toolpaths only: the width of the picture.

fields.name: Height
fields.text: Older toolpaths only: the height of the picture.

fields.name: Start Depth (D)
fields.text: How far below the surface carving starts; usually 0.

fields.name: Flat Depth (F)
fields.text: Tick to limit how deep the cut goes; unticked, the V goes as deep as each line needs.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: A V-bit, engraving tool, ball nose or tapered ball nose. Select... picks one.

fields.name: Machining Limit Boundary
fields.text: Where to sketch: the Bitmap or Model Boundary, Selected Vector(s) or a Selected Level.

fields.name: Level
fields.text: With Selected Level: the level whose components limit the sketch.

fields.name: Boundary Offset
fields.text: Grows the boundary outward by this much; negative shrinks it.

fields.name: Line Thickness
fields.text: Slider from Thin to Thick: how heavy the traced sketch lines are. The preview counts the areas found.

fields.name: Project toolpath onto 3D model
fields.text: Measures depths down from the model surface instead of the flat top.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Manual uses the vectors you select; Selector... picks them with filters.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The toolpath's name in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the sketch toolpath. It needs a carving tool.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Calculated toolpaths stay.

steps: Choose Bitmap and select the picture in the 2D view, or choose 3D Model.
Pick a V-bit or ball nose.
Set the boundary and move Line Thickness until the preview looks right.
Press Calculate.

laserSketchToolpath.summary: Finds the key lines of a bitmap or of the 3D model and burns them as hatching with a laser, for a pencil sketch look.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: The laser tool. Select... picks one; it must be a laser.

fields.name: Selection
fields.text: Sketch a Bitmap selected in the 2D view, or the 3D Model.

fields.name: Left (X)
fields.text: Older toolpaths that read an image file only: the left edge of the picture.

fields.name: Bottom (Y)
fields.text: Older toolpaths only: the bottom edge of the picture.

fields.name: Width
fields.text: Older toolpaths only: the width of the picture.

fields.name: Height
fields.text: Older toolpaths only: the height of the picture.

fields.name: Power
fields.text: Laser power in percent. Leave empty to use the tool's setting.

fields.name: Overscan
fields.text: How far each hatch line runs past the sketch, so the laser burns evenly.

fields.name: Machining Limit Boundary
fields.text: Where to sketch: the Bitmap or Model Boundary, Selected Vector(s) or a Selected Level.

fields.name: Level
fields.text: With Selected Level: the level whose components limit the sketch.

fields.name: Boundary Offset
fields.text: Grows the boundary outward by this much; negative shrinks it.

fields.name: Line Thickness
fields.text: Slider from Thin to Thick: how heavy the traced sketch lines are. The preview counts the areas found.

fields.name: Stepover
fields.text: The distance between hatch lines.

fields.name: Hatch Angle
fields.text: The angle of the hatch lines, in degrees.

fields.name: Strategy
fields.text: Fill Together crosses the whole sketch; Fill Regionally does each area; within Vectors also keeps travel on the lines.

fields.name: Cross Hatch
fields.text: Adds a second set of hatch lines across the first.

fields.name: Project toolpath onto 3D model
fields.text: Measures depths down from the model surface instead of the flat top.

fields.name: Vector Selection
fields.text: Manual uses the vectors you select; Selector... picks them with filters.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The toolpath's name in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the laser sketch toolpath. It needs a laser tool.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Calculated toolpaths stay.

steps: Choose Bitmap and select the picture in the 2D view, or choose 3D Model.
Pick a laser tool and set the power.
Move Line Thickness until the preview looks right.
Set the hatch stepover and angle, then press Calculate.

laserPictureToolpath.summary: Burns the bitmap selected in the drawing with a laser along raster or hatch lines, or along selected vectors. Each dot gets a power from its gray level, or is dithered fully on or off.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: The laser tool. Select... picks one; it must be a laser.

fields.name: Power
fields.text: Laser power in percent for the darkest parts. Leave empty to use the tool's setting.

fields.name: Move Speed
fields.text: How fast the laser moves while burning. Leave empty to use the tool's setting.

fields.name: No. Passes
fields.text: How many times the picture is burned.

fields.name: Overscan
fields.text: Runs each line a little past the picture, as a percent, so the laser burns evenly to the edge.

fields.name: Strategy
fields.text: Raster burns parallel lines, Hatch burns crossing lines, Selected Vectors burns along your vectors.

fields.name: Dither Image
fields.text: Burns each dot fully on or off in a dot pattern instead of varying the power.

fields.name: Line Spacing
fields.text: Slider from Dense to Sparse: the distance between burn lines. Match it to your laser's dot size.

fields.name: Line Angle
fields.text: The angle of the burn lines, in degrees. Off with Selected Vectors.

fields.name: Project toolpath onto 3D model
fields.text: Follows the model surface instead of the flat top.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The toolpath's name in the toolpath list.

fields.name: Calculate
fields.text: Makes the picture toolpath. It needs a selected bitmap and a laser tool.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Calculated toolpaths stay.

fields.name: Immediate Output
fields.text: Machine, Post Processor and Save Toolpath(s) ... save this toolpath right after calculating it.

steps: Select the bitmap to burn, and vectors if you want to burn along them.
Pick a laser tool and set power and speed.
Choose raster or hatch, the line spacing and angle.
Press Calculate, then save it for your laser.

assemblyView.summary: Puts the machined parts together in the 3D view so you can check how they fit before cutting. Each part the toolpaths cut free becomes a piece you can move, mate, measure and check.

fields.name: How to build your own assembly
fields.text: Four steps from a drawing to an exploded view: draw the parts, cut them free with toolpaths, join them, then check the fit and explode. Open while the job has no pieces.

fields.name: Joint Creator
fields.text: Opens the Joint Creator to cut matching joints between two parts. Open the Assembly View again afterward to see them together.

fields.name: Snap to nearby pieces
fields.text: Makes a moved piece snap to faces of the pieces near it.

fields.name: Pieces
fields.text: Lists the pieces; buttons on each row show, hide, isolate or ground it. Show All shows them all.

fields.name: Remove Piece
fields.text: Takes an added component piece back out of the view.

fields.name: Mates
fields.text: Lists the mates between pieces; edit, suppress or delete each one.

fields.name: Add Component
fields.text: Brings a component from the Component Tree in as its own piece, such as a bought part.

fields.name: Piece from
fields.text: Use the Machined simulation of the sheet or its Raw model for the picked piece.

fields.name: Position
fields.text: Type the picked piece's X, Y and Z position, then press Apply.

fields.name: Rotation
fields.text: Type the picked piece's turn about X, Y and Z in degrees, then press Apply.

fields.name: Mate Pieces
fields.text: Pick a mate type, then Pick Faces: first the face that stays, then the face that moves.

fields.name: Target clearance
fields.text: Fit: the gap you want between parts that fit together.

fields.name: Tolerance (±)
fields.text: Fit: how far a gap may differ from the target and still be OK.

fields.name: Include hidden pieces
fields.text: Fit: checks hidden pieces too; clear it to check only the pieces shown.

fields.name: Verify Fit
fields.text: Measures every joint on the exact cut edges and marks each OK, Loose, Tight or Interference.

fields.name: Show Fit
fields.text: Colors the joints in the 3D view by how well they fit.

fields.name: Explode
fields.text: Slider that moves the pieces apart out of their joints; Explode Steps sets named moves.

fields.name: Cut the pieces with a plane
fields.text: Section: slices the view so you can see inside the assembly.

fields.name: Plane across
fields.text: Section: which axis the cutting plane lies across.

fields.name: Offset
fields.text: Section: moves the cutting plane along its axis.

fields.name: Flip (keep the other side)
fields.text: Section: shows the other side of the plane.

fields.name: Pick Points
fields.text: Measure: click two points on the pieces to get the distance between them.

fields.name: Cut List
fields.text: Lists each piece with its count, length, width and thickness; Refresh updates it.

fields.name: Export CSV
fields.text: Saves the cut list as a CSV file.

fields.name: Format
fields.text: The file type for Export Assembly: STL or 3MF.

fields.name: Export Assembly...
fields.text: Saves the assembled pieces as a 3D file.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form and gives the 3D view back to the job.

steps: Calculate the toolpaths that cut your parts free.
Open Assembly View; each cut part appears as a piece.
Click a piece and drag its arrows and rings, or mate its faces to another piece.
Press Verify Fit to check the joints.
Drag the Explode slider under Pieces to pull the parts apart; use Section and Measure to inspect, then export the cut list.

furnitureDesigner.summary: Designs a piece of furniture from a template: type its sizes, pick its joints and see it in the Assembly View as you go. Create makes the panels on sheets, the joints, the toolpaths and the pieces; Update makes them again after a change.

fields.name: Name
fields.text: The design's name; its layer and sheets are named after it.

fields.name: Sizes and layout
fields.text: The template's settings by group. Boxes take calculations; the slider under a size or count drags it. The preview follows at once and a made design is made again when you stop.

fields.name: Style
fields.text: Picks a joint for every kind of connection at once: Traditional, Flat pack, Quick build, Laser and thin stock, or Glue and screws.

fields.name: Joint rows
fields.text: One row per kind of connection, such as Shelves to sides, with the joints valid there. Edit joint sizes changes their count, depth or diameter; empty boxes use the sizes worked out for the stock.

fields.name: Fit and tool
fields.text: The fit, corner relief and tool every joint shares with the Joint Creator.

fields.name: Cut List, Hardware, Estimate
fields.text: The panels with their finished sizes, the screws, dowels and fittings to buy, and the sheets and cutting time. Export CSV saves each list.

fields.name: Seams
fields.text: Hover a seam in the Assembly View to see its joint; click it to pick another, or tick Use for all like this to change every seam of its kind.

fields.name: Save as Template
fields.text: Keeps the design in your library with its sizes as the new defaults.

fields.name: Remove
fields.text: Takes the design, with its panels, joints, toolpaths and pieces, out of the job.

steps: In the Assembly View press New Furniture and pick a template.
Type the sizes or drag the sliders; pick a joinery style.
Press Create, then click any seam to change its joint.

jointCreator.summary: Joins two flat parts with a joint the end mill cuts from the top, such as fingers, dados, tabs, dovetails or dowels. Pick a joint, click the edge of one part and the edge or face of the other, check the preview and press Create.

fields.name: Joint
fields.text: The gallery of joint types; click one to use it. Each shows a one line description.

fields.name: Box from Selection
fields.text: Joins the selected panels at every matching edge at once.

fields.name: First part
fields.text: Shows the edge picked on the first part, or not picked. Esc or Pick again starts over.

fields.name: Second part
fields.text: Shows the edge, or the place on the face, picked on the second part.

fields.name: From the edge
fields.text: For joints on a face, such as a dado: exactly how far in from the edge the joint sits.

fields.name: Pattern
fields.text: Living Hinge only: Straight, Sinuous or Spiral slots, each bending differently.

fields.name: Count
fields.text: The joint's own sizes, such as Count, Width and Depth. Fields showing auto are sized for you.

fields.name: Fits one way only
fields.text: Makes the first finger or tab wider so the parts go together only one way.

fields.name: More
fields.text: Extra settings for the joint, such as corners, tab ends, blind or through, and the tool.

fields.name: Tool
fields.text: In More: the end mill the joint is sized for; relief and fingers follow its diameter.

fields.name: Fit
fields.text: All joints: Slip, Press, Glue, Knock-down or Custom, each with its clearance per side.

fields.name: Clearance a side
fields.text: Custom fit: the gap left on each side of a joint.

fields.name: Corner relief
fields.text: None, Dog-bone or T-bone cuts into inside corners so square parts fit despite the round tool.

fields.name: Thickness
fields.text: The measured stock thickness; measure your material and type it for a good fit.

fields.name: Assembled
fields.text: A 3D preview of the parts joined; the Explode slider pulls them apart.

fields.name: Make the toolpaths too
fields.text: Also makes the toolpaths to cut the joint when you press Create.

fields.name: Create
fields.text: Makes the joint on both parts as one undo step. It reads Apply when editing a joint.

fields.name: Remove Joint
fields.text: Takes the joint off and puts both edges back as they were.

fields.name: Test Coupon
fields.text: Makes a small sample of this joint to cut first and check the fit.

fields.name: Joints in this job
fields.text: Lists every joint; click one to edit it.

fields.name: Close
fields.text: Closes the form. Joints made stay.

steps: Pick a joint type from the gallery.
Click the edge of the first part.
Click the matching edge, or the place on the face, of the second part.
Set the fit, relief and measured thickness, and check the preview.
Press Create, then cut a Test Coupon first if you are unsure of the fit.
